title.raw: 卷47 盧玄 Volume 47: Lu Xuan

sentences.zh: 盧玄，字子真，范陽涿人也。

translations.literal: Lu Xuan, whose style name was Zizhen, was a native of Zhuo in Fanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Xuan, style name Zizhen, was from Zhuo in Fanyang.

sentences.zh: 曾袓諶，晉司空劉琨從事中郎。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Chen served as Registrar under Liu Kun, Minister of Works of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Chen had been Registrar to Liu Kun, Minister of Works under the Jin.

sentences.zh: 袓偃，父邈，並仕慕容氏為郡太守，皆以儒雅稱。

translations.literal: His grandfather Yan and father Miao both served the Murong as commandery governors and were all praised for scholarly refinement.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Yan and his father Miao both held commandery governorships under the Murong, and both were known for their scholarly elegance.

sentences.zh: 神䴥四年，辟召儒儁，以玄為首，授中書博士。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Shenqi, eminent Confucian scholars were summoned; Xuan was placed first and appointed Doctor of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Shenqi, when the court called up eminent Confucian scholars, Xuan was ranked first and appointed Doctor of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 司徒崔浩，玄之外兄，每與玄言，輒歎曰：「對子真，使我懷古之情更深。

translations.literal: Cui Hao, Grand Mentor, was Xuan's maternal cousin; whenever he spoke with Xuan he would sigh and say: "Facing Zizhen makes my longing for antiquity grow deeper."
translations.idiomatic: Cui Hao, Grand Mentor and Xuan's cousin on his mother's side, would sigh whenever they spoke together: "In Zizhen's company my longing for the ancients only deepens."

sentences.zh: 」浩大欲齊整人倫，分明姓族。

translations.literal: Hao greatly wished to regularize human relations and clarify clans and lineages.
translations.idiomatic: Hao was deeply intent on standardizing human relations and sorting out clan distinctions.

sentences.zh: 玄勸之曰：「夫創制立事，各有其時，樂為此者，詎幾人也？

translations.literal: Xuan admonished him, saying: "Establishing institutions and undertaking affairs each has its proper season; how many are there who delight in such work?"
translations.idiomatic: Xuan urged him: "Creating institutions and launching enterprises each has its season—how many would truly relish such an undertaking?"

sentences.zh: 宜其三思。

translations.literal: One ought to think three times about it.
translations.idiomatic: You should weigh it again and again.

sentences.zh: 」浩當時雖無異言，竟不納，浩敗頗亦由此。

translations.literal: Although Hao had no dissenting words at the time, he ultimately did not accept this advice; Hao's downfall stemmed in considerable part from this.
translations.idiomatic: Hao offered no objection at the time, yet he never took the advice—and in no small measure his fall came of this.

sentences.zh: 後轉寧朔將軍、兼散騎常侍，使劉義隆。

translations.literal: Later he was transferred to General Who Pacifies the North and concurrent Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, and was sent as envoy to Liu Yilong.
translations.idiomatic: He was later promoted to General Who Pacifies the North and concurrent Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, and sent on embassy to Liu Yilong.

sentences.zh: 義隆見之，與語良久，歎曰：「中郎，卿曾袓也。

translations.literal: Yilong met him and spoke with him at length, sighing: "Attendant, your great-grandfather was—"
translations.idiomatic: Yilong received him and talked with him for a long while, then sighed: "Attendant, that was your great-grandfather."

sentences.zh: 」既還，病卒。

translations.literal: When he had returned, he died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: After he returned home, he fell ill and died.

sentences.zh: 子度世，字子遷。

translations.literal: His son was Du Shi, whose style name was Ziqian.
translations.idiomatic: His son Du Shi bore the style name Ziqian.

sentences.zh: 幼而聰達，有計數。

translations.literal: From childhood he was clever and perspicacious, with a gift for strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Clever and far-seeing from boyhood, he had a knack for calculation.

sentences.zh: 為中書學生，應選東宮。

translations.literal: He served as a student of the Secretariat and was selected for the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He studied at the Secretariat and was chosen for service in the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 弱冠，與從兄遐俱以學行為時流所重。

translations.literal: At his coming of age, he and his cousin Xia were both esteemed by the leading men of the day for their learning and conduct.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached manhood, he and his cousin Xia were both held in high regard by the leading scholars of the age for their learning and character.

sentences.zh: 度世後以崔浩事，棄官逃於高陽鄭羆家，羆匿之。

translations.literal: Later, because of the Cui Hao affair, Du Shi abandoned his office and fled to the home of Zheng Pi of Gaoyang, who concealed him.
translations.idiomatic: Later, implicated in the Cui Hao affair, Du Shi resigned his post and fled to the home of Zheng Pi of Gaoyang, who hid him.

sentences.zh: 使者囚羆長子，將加捶楚。

translations.literal: The envoys imprisoned Pi's eldest son and were about to apply beating and torture.
translations.idiomatic: The authorities seized Pi's eldest son and were about to beat and torture him.

sentences.zh: 羆戒之曰：「君子殺身以成人，汝雖死勿言。

translations.literal: Pi warned him: "A gentleman gives his life to complete another's integrity; though you die, do not speak."
translations.idiomatic: Pi admonished him: "A gentleman lays down his life to preserve another's honor—even if you die, say nothing."

sentences.zh: 」子奉父命，遂被考掠，至乃火爇其體，因以物故，卒無所言。

translations.literal: The son obeyed his father's charge, was put to torture, and they even burned his body with fire until he died, yet in the end he said nothing.
translations.idiomatic: The son obeyed his father's command. He was tortured and even burned with fire until he died, yet to the end he revealed nothing.

sentences.zh: 度世後令弟娶羆妹，以報其恩。

translations.literal: Later Du Shi had his younger brother marry Pi's sister to repay his kindness.
translations.idiomatic: Du Shi later had his younger brother marry Pi's sister to repay the debt of gratitude.

sentences.zh: 世袓臨江，劉義隆使其殿中將軍黃延年朝貢。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizu crossed the Yangzi, Liu Yilong sent his Palace General Huang Yannian to pay tribute.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizu crossed the Yangzi, Liu Yilong sent his Palace General Huang Yannian to present tribute.

sentences.zh: 世袓問延年曰：「范陽盧度世坐與崔浩親通，逃命江表，應已至彼？

translations.literal: The Emperor asked Yannian: "Lu Du Shi of Fanyang, implicated for close ties with Cui Hao, fled for his life to the lands south of the Yangzi—he should have arrived there by now?"
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor asked Yannian: "Lu Du Shi of Fanyang, charged with close ties to Cui Hao, fled south of the Yangzi for his life—surely he has reached your realm by now?"

sentences.zh: 」延對曰：「都下無聞，當必不至。

translations.literal: Yannian replied: "There is no report in the capital region; he surely has not gone there."
translations.idiomatic: Yannian answered: "We have heard nothing of him in our capital; he surely has not come."

sentences.zh: 」世袓詔東宮赦度世宗族逃亡及籍沒者。

translations.literal: The Emperor issued an edict through the Eastern Palace pardoning Du Shi's clan for flight and for families whose registers had been confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor then ordered the Eastern Palace to pardon Du Shi's kinsmen who had fled and those whose households had been confiscated.

sentences.zh: 度世乃出。

translations.literal: Du Shi then came forth.
translations.idiomatic: Only then did Du Shi emerge from hiding.

sentences.zh: 赴京，拜中書侍郎，襲爵。

translations.literal: He went to the capital, was appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat, and inherited the noble rank.
translations.idiomatic: He went to the capital, was appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat, and inherited the family title.

sentences.zh: 初，玄有五子，嫡唯度世，餘皆別生。

translations.literal: At first Xuan had five sons; only Du Shi was born of the principal wife, the rest were by secondary consorts.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan had had five sons in all; only Du Shi was born of the principal wife, the others of concubines.

sentences.zh: 崔浩事難，其庶兄弟常欲危害之，度世常深忿恨。

translations.literal: When the Cui Hao crisis struck, his half-brothers often wished to harm him, and Du Shi bore deep resentment.
translations.idiomatic: During the Cui Hao affair his half-brothers had often sought to do him harm, and Du Shi harbored deep resentment.

sentences.zh: 及度世有子，每誡約令絕妾孽，不得使長，以防後患。

translations.literal: When Du Shi had sons of his own, he repeatedly admonished them to cut off secondary sons and not let them grow up, to guard against later trouble.
translations.idiomatic: When Du Shi himself had sons, he repeatedly warned them to disown sons born to concubines and not let them grow up, lest trouble arise later.

sentences.zh: 至淵兄弟，婢賤生子，雖形貌相類，皆不舉接。

translations.literal: When it came to Yuan and his brothers, though sons born to maidservants resembled them in appearance, they would not acknowledge them.
translations.idiomatic: By the time of Yuan and his brothers, even when sons born to servant girls resembled them in looks, they would not acknowledge them.

sentences.zh: 為識者所非。

translations.literal: This was censured by those in the know.
translations.idiomatic: Men of judgment condemned this practice.

sentences.zh: 淵，字伯源，小名陽烏。

translations.literal: Yuan, whose style name was Boyuan, had the childhood name Yangwu.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan, style name Boyuan, was called Yangwu as a child.

sentences.zh: 性溫雅寡欲，有袓父之風，敦尚學業，閨門和睦。

translations.literal: His nature was gentle, refined, and free of excess desire; he had the manner of his grandfather, cherished scholarship, and kept his household harmonious.
translations.idiomatic: Gentle, refined, and sparing of desire, he bore his grandfather's manner, devoted himself to learning, and kept his household at peace.

sentences.zh: 襲侯爵，拜主客令，典屬國。

translations.literal: He inherited the marquisate, was appointed Director of Guests, and oversaw dependent states.
translations.idiomatic: He inherited the marquisate, was appointed Director of Guests, and supervised the dependent states.

sentences.zh: 遷祕書令、始平王師。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Director of the Secretariat and Preceptor to the Prince of Shiping.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Director of the Secretariat and Preceptor to the Prince of Shiping.

sentences.zh: 以例降爵為伯。

translations.literal: By established regulation his noble rank was reduced to Count.
translations.idiomatic: Under the usual rules his title was reduced from marquis to count.

sentences.zh: 給事黃門侍郎，遷兼散騎常侍、祕書監、本州大中正。

translations.literal: Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Yellow Gate; later concurrently Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, Supervisor of the Secretariat, and Chief Rectifier of his native province.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Yellow Gate, then was promoted to concurrent Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, Supervisor of the Secretariat, and Chief Rectifier of his home province.

sentences.zh: 是時，高祖將立馮后，方集朝臣議之。

translations.literal: At this time Gaozu was about to install Lady Feng as empress and had gathered the court ministers to deliberate.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Emperor Gaozu was about to install Lady Feng as empress and had summoned the court to discuss it.

sentences.zh: 高祖先謂淵曰：「卿意以為何如？

translations.literal: Gaozu first asked Yuan: "What is your opinion?"
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu first asked Yuan: "What do you think?"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「此自古所慎，如臣愚意，宜更簡卜。

translations.literal: He replied: "This is what antiquity has always treated with caution; in this servant's humble view, one should further select by divination."
translations.idiomatic: He answered: "This is what the ancients always treated with caution; in my humble view, the choice should be tested further by divination."

sentences.zh: 」高祖曰：「以先后之姪，朕意已定。

translations.literal: Gaozu said: "As the former empress's niece, my mind is already settled."
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu said: "As the former empress's niece, my mind is already made up."

sentences.zh: 」淵曰：「雖奉敕如此，然於臣心實有未盡。

translations.literal: Yuan said: "Though I have received such an edict, in my heart I am not fully at ease."
translations.idiomatic: Yuan said: "Though I have received Your Majesty's command, my heart is not wholly at ease."

sentences.zh: 」及朝臣集議，執意如前。

translations.literal: When the ministers assembled to discuss, he held to his view as before.
translations.idiomatic: When the ministers met to deliberate, he held to the same view as before.

sentences.zh: 馮誕有盛寵，深以為恨，淵不以介懷。

translations.literal: Feng Dan enjoyed great favor and deeply resented this, but Yuan did not take it to heart.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Dan, who enjoyed great favor, resented this deeply, but Yuan gave it no thought.

sentences.zh: 及高祖議伐蕭賾，淵表曰：

translations.literal: When Gaozu debated campaigning against Xiao Ze, Yuan submitted a memorial stating:
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu deliberated a campaign against Xiao Ze, Yuan submitted a memorial that read:

sentences.zh: 臣誠識不周覽，頗尋篇籍。

translations.literal: This servant's knowledge is truly not comprehensive, yet I have searched through the written records.
translations.idiomatic: My own knowledge is far from complete, yet I have searched the written records.

sentences.zh: 自魏晉以前，承平之世，未有皇輿親御六軍，決勝行陳之間者。

translations.literal: From before Wei and Jin through ages of peace, there has never been an imperial carriage personally commanding the six armies to decide victory amid the battle lines.
translations.idiomatic: Before Wei and Jin, in ages of peace, no emperor ever personally led the six armies to decide victory on the battlefield.

sentences.zh: 勝不足為武，弗勝有虧威德，明千鈞之弩不為鼷鼠發機故也。

translations.literal: Victory is insufficient to count as martial prowess, while defeat damages prestige and virtue—clearly a crossbow of a thousand jun does not release its trigger for a mouse, for this reason.
translations.idiomatic: Victory would add little to one's martial renown, while defeat would injure imperial prestige—just as a crossbow of a thousand jun is not drawn for a mouse.

sentences.zh: 昔魏武以弊卒一萬而袁紹土崩，謝玄以步兵三千而苻堅瓦解。

translations.literal: Formerly Cao Wu with ten thousand worn troops made Yuan Shao's host collapse; Xie Xuan with three thousand foot soldiers made Fu Jian disintegrate.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao once routed Yuan Shao with ten thousand weary troops; Xie Xuan shattered Fu Jian's host with three thousand foot soldiers.

sentences.zh: 勝負不由眾寡，成敗在於須臾，若用田豐之謀，則坐制孟德矣。

translations.literal: Victory and defeat do not depend on numbers many or few; success and failure hang on a moment—had Tian Feng's plan been used, Cao Mengde would have been controlled while seated.
translations.idiomatic: Victory does not depend on numbers; the issue is decided in an instant—had Yuan Shao followed Tian Feng's counsel, he would have held Cao Cao at his mercy without stirring.

sentences.zh: 魏既并蜀，迄于晉世，吳介有江水，居其上流，大小勢殊，德政理絕。

translations.literal: After Wei had annexed Shu, down through the Jin age Wu alone had the Yangzi as a barrier and held the upper reaches; great and small were disparate in power, and virtue and governance were utterly different.
translations.idiomatic: After Wei annexed Shu, through the Jin dynasty Wu alone had the Yangzi as its barrier and held the upper reaches; the two states differed vastly in scale, and in virtue and governance they were worlds apart.

sentences.zh: 然猶君臣協謀，垂數十載。

translations.literal: Yet ruler and ministers still coordinated their plans, and this lasted for several decades.
translations.idiomatic: Yet ruler and ministers still worked in concert, and the contest dragged on for decades.

sentences.zh: 逮孫皓暴戾，上下攜爽，水陸俱進，一舉始克。

translations.literal: Only when Sun Hao became cruel and tyrannical, so that above and below were at odds, did advance by land and water together conquer them in a single stroke.
translations.idiomatic: Only when Sun Hao turned cruel and tyrannical, alienating court and people alike, did a combined land-and-water advance conquer Wu in one stroke.

sentences.zh: 今蕭氏以篡殺之燼，政虐役繁，又支屬相屠，人神同棄。

translations.literal: Now the Xiao house rests on the embers of usurpation and slaughter; government is cruel and corvée labor heavy; moreover collateral branches slaughter one another—men and spirits alike have cast them off.
translations.idiomatic: The Xiao regime now rests on the ashes of usurpation and murder; its government is cruel and its levies crushing; its own kin turn on one another, and both men and gods have abandoned them.

sentences.zh: 吳會之民，延踵皇澤，正是齊軌之期，一同之會。

translations.literal: The people of Wu and Kuaiji crane their necks for the imperial grace—this is precisely the season to align with our track and the moment for unification.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Wu and Kuaiji yearn for the imperial grace; this is the moment to bring them into one fold and achieve unification.

sentences.zh: 若大駕南巡，必左袵革面，閩越倒戈，其猶運山壓卵，有征無戰。

translations.literal: If the imperial carriage tours south, they will surely turn their lapels left and change their faces; Min and Yue will cast aside their weapons—it will be like moving a mountain onto an egg; there will be a campaign but no fighting.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty tours south in person, the southerners will surely turn their coats and change their allegiance; Fujian and Yue will lay down their arms—it will be like crushing an egg with a mountain; there will be a campaign but no battle.

sentences.zh: 然愚謂萬乘親戎，轉漕難繼，千里饋糧，士有飢色，大軍之後，必有凶年。

translations.literal: Yet in this servant's view, when the Son of Heaven personally takes the field, transport of grain is hard to sustain; feeding armies a thousand li away leaves the troops hungry, and after a great host passes there is sure to be a famine year.
translations.idiomatic: Yet I believe that when the sovereign takes the field in person, supply lines cannot be sustained; armies fed from a thousand li away go hungry, and in the wake of a great host famine follows.

sentences.zh: 不若命將簡銳，盪滌江右，然後鳴鸞巡省，告成東岳，則天下幸甚，率土戴賴。

translations.literal: Better to commission generals with picked elite troops to sweep the lands east of the Yangzi, and only then sound the imperial carriage on a tour of inspection and report success at the Eastern Peak—then all under Heaven would be greatly blessed and the realm would rely on Your grace.
translations.idiomatic: Better to send generals with picked troops to sweep the lands east of the Yangzi, and only then let Your Majesty tour in state and report victory at Mount Tai—then all under Heaven would be blessed and the realm would rejoice in Your rule.

sentences.zh: 臣又聞流言，關右之民，自比年以來，競設齋會，假稱豪貴，以相扇惑。

translations.literal: This servant has also heard rumors that among the people west of the Pass, in recent years they vie to hold fasting assemblies, falsely claiming to be great and noble, to incite one another.
translations.idiomatic: I have also heard rumors that in recent years the people west of the Pass have vied to hold fasting assemblies, falsely posing as great families, to stir one another up.

sentences.zh: 顯然於眾坐之中，以謗朝廷。

translations.literal: Openly, in the midst of public gatherings, they slander the court.
translations.idiomatic: Openly, before assembled crowds, they slander the court.

sentences.zh: 無上之心，莫此之甚。

translations.literal: Disloyalty to superiors—nothing exceeds this.
translations.idiomatic: Disloyalty to the throne—nothing could be more extreme.

sentences.zh: 愚謂宜速懲絕，戮其魁帥。

translations.literal: In this servant's view one should swiftly punish and cut them off, executing their ringleaders.
translations.idiomatic: I believe they should be swiftly suppressed and their ringleaders executed.

sentences.zh: 不爾懼成黃巾、赤眉之禍。

translations.literal: Otherwise I fear it will become the calamity of the Yellow Turbans and the Red Eyebrows.
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise I fear we shall see another Yellow Turban or Red Eyebrow rebellion.

sentences.zh: 育其微萌，不芟之毫末，斧斤一加，恐蹈害者眾。

translations.literal: Nurture the slightest sprout and do not cut it at the tip of a blade—when axe and adze are applied once, I fear many will suffer harm.
translations.idiomatic: If the first shoots are allowed to grow and are not cut down at once, when the axe finally falls many will suffer.

sentences.zh: 臣世奉皇家，義均休戚，誠知干忤之愆實深，然不忠之罪莫大。

translations.literal: This servant's family has served the imperial house for generations; in righteousness we share fortune and misfortune alike. I truly know that the offense of presumption is deep, yet the crime of disloyalty is greater still.
translations.idiomatic: My family has served the imperial house for generations; our fortunes are bound to the throne. I know well that to speak thus is presumptuous, yet the greater crime would be disloyal silence.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：

translations.literal: An edict stated:
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor replied in an edict:

sentences.zh: 至德雖一，樹功多途。

translations.literal: Supreme virtue is one, yet establishing merit has many paths.
translations.idiomatic: Supreme virtue is one, but merit may be won by many paths.

sentences.zh: 三聖殊文，五帝異律，或張或弛，豈必相因。

translations.literal: The Three Sage Kings had different writings; the Five Emperors had different laws—sometimes tight, sometimes loose; must one necessarily follow another?
translations.idiomatic: The Three Sage Kings wrote differently; the Five Emperors ruled differently—sometimes strict, sometimes lenient. Must one age simply copy another?

sentences.zh: 遠惟承平之主，所主不親旆五戎者，蓋有由矣。

translations.literal: Reflecting far back on rulers of peaceful ages who did not personally banner the five armies—there were reasons for this.
translations.idiomatic: Looking back at peaceful rulers who did not personally lead the five armies, there were reasons for that too.

sentences.zh: 英明之主，或以同軌無征；

translations.literal: Brilliant rulers sometimes refrained from campaigning because all shared the same track;
translations.idiomatic: Wise rulers sometimes refrained from war because the realm was already united;

sentences.zh: 守庸之君，或緣志劣寢伐。

translations.literal: mediocre rulers who kept the throne sometimes let their ambitions languish and abandoned campaigning.
translations.idiomatic: mediocre ones sometimes lacked the will and let martial ambition sleep.

sentences.zh: 今若喻之英皇，時非昔類；

translations.literal: If one compares me now to those brilliant emperors, the times are not of the same kind;
translations.idiomatic: Compare me now to those brilliant emperors and the times are not the same;

sentences.zh: 比之庸后，意有恧焉。

translations.literal: compare me to mediocre successors and I feel shame in my intent.
translations.idiomatic: compare me to mediocre successors and I would be ashamed.

sentences.zh: 脫元極之尊，本不宜駕，二公之徒，革輅之戎，寧非謬歟？

translations.literal: Setting aside the honor of the supreme pole, it is fundamentally unsuitable to take the reins—men like the Two Dukes in leather chariots going to war, is this not absurd?
translations.idiomatic: Apart from the dignity of the throne itself, is it not absurd for men like the Duke of Zhou to go to war in a leather chariot?

sentences.zh: 尋夫昔人，若必須己而濟世，豈不克廣先業也。

translations.literal: Searching among the men of old, if one must rely on oneself to save the age, how could one not be able to extend the work of one's forebears?
translations.idiomatic: Consider the ancients: if saving the age required one's own hand, how could one fail to enlarge the inheritance of one's fathers?

sentences.zh: 定火之雄，[1]未聞不武，世袓之行，匪皆疑懾。

translations.literal: The hero who settled the fire—none have heard he was not martial; the deeds of Emperor Shizu were not all met with doubt and fear.
translations.idiomatic: The hero who settled the mandate of Zhou was hardly unwarlike; Emperor Shizu's campaigns were not all met with doubt and dread.

sentences.zh: 且曹操勝袁，蓋由德義內舉；

translations.literal: Moreover Cao Cao's victory over Yuan came largely from virtue and righteousness raised within;
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao's victory over Yuan Shao owed much to moral authority won at home;

sentences.zh: 苻堅瓦解，當緣立政未至。

translations.literal: Fu Jian's collapse was surely because his establishment of government had not reached completion.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian's collapse came because his government had not yet been firmly established.

sentences.zh: 定非弊卒之力強，十萬之眾寡也。

translations.literal: It was certainly not that worn troops were strong or that a host of a hundred thousand was few.
translations.idiomatic: It was surely not a matter of worn troops being strong or a hundred thousand men being few.

sentences.zh: 今則驅馳先天之術，駕用仁義之師，審觀成敗，庶免斯咎。

translations.literal: Now we shall drive forward the arts that precede Heaven and employ an army of benevolence and righteousness, carefully observing success and failure, so as hopefully to avoid this fault.
translations.idiomatic: Now we shall advance by the arts that precede Heaven and lead an army of benevolence and righteousness, weighing success and failure carefully, so as to avoid that error.

sentences.zh: 長江之阻，未足可憚；

translations.literal: The barrier of the Long River is not enough to be feared;
translations.idiomatic: The Yangzi's barrier is nothing to fear;

sentences.zh: 踰紀之略，何必可師。

translations.literal: strategies that span more than an age—why must they be taken as models?
translations.idiomatic: and strategies from ages past need not be our only guide.

sentences.zh: 洞庭、彭蠡，竟非殷固，奮臂一呼，或成漢業。

translations.literal: Dongting and Poyang were after all not impregnable as Yin; raise the arm and call once, and the Han enterprise may be accomplished.
translations.idiomatic: Dongting and Poyang were not impregnable fortresses of Yin; one cry and the Han cause may be won.

sentences.zh: 經略之義，當付之臨機；

translations.literal: The principles of strategy should be entrusted to the moment of action;
translations.idiomatic: Strategy must be left to the moment of decision;

sentences.zh: 足食之籌，望寄之蕭相。

translations.literal: plans for full bellies I look to entrust to the Chancellor Xiao.
translations.idiomatic: and plans for provisioning I entrust to my Xiao He.

sentences.zh: 將希混一，豈好輕動，利見之事，何得委人也！

translations.literal: About to hope for unification, how could I delight in rash movement? When benefit is seen, how can it be delegated to others!
translations.idiomatic: I seek unification—how could I delight in rash action? When the moment of advantage appears, how can I leave it to another!

sentences.zh: 又水旱之運，未必由兵；

translations.literal: Moreover the cycles of flood and drought are not necessarily caused by armies;
translations.idiomatic: Floods and droughts are not necessarily caused by war;

sentences.zh: 堯湯之難，詎因興旅？

translations.literal: the hardships of Yao and Tang—how could they be because troops were raised?
translations.idiomatic: the trials of Yao and Tang were hardly caused by raising armies.

sentences.zh: 頗豐之後，雖靜有之，關左小紛，已敕禁勒。

translations.literal: After abundant harvests, though calm may sometimes occur, the minor disturbances west of the Pass have already been ordered forbidden and restrained.
translations.idiomatic: After good harvests quiet may return; the minor disturbances west of the Pass have already been ordered suppressed.

sentences.zh: 流言之細，曷足以紆天功。

translations.literal: The minutiae of floating rumors—how could they suffice to obstruct Heaven's achievement?
translations.idiomatic: Petty rumors are hardly enough to obstruct the imperial enterprise.

sentences.zh: 深錄誠心，勿恨不相遂耳。

translations.literal: I deeply record your sincere heart; do not resent that we do not go the same way.
translations.idiomatic: I deeply appreciate your sincerity; do not resent that we cannot follow the same course.

sentences.zh: 及車駕南伐，趙郡王幹督關右諸軍事，詔加淵使持節、安南將軍為副，勒眾七萬將出子午。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage campaigned south, the Prince of Zhao Commandery Gan supervised all military affairs west of the Pass; an edict added Yuan as Bearer of the Staff of Authority and General Who Pacifies the South as deputy, leading a host of seventy thousand about to exit through Ziwu.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor marched south, Prince Gan of Zhao Commandery supervised all military affairs west of the Pass; Yuan was appointed Bearer of the Staff and General Who Pacifies the South as his deputy, leading seventy thousand men to march out through Ziwu Pass.

sentences.zh: 尋以蕭賾死，停師。

translations.literal: Soon, because Xiao Ze died, the army halted.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Xiao Ze died and the campaign was halted.

sentences.zh: 是時涇州羌叛，殘破城邑，淵以步騎六千眾號三萬，徐行而進。

translations.literal: At this time the Qiang of Jing Province rebelled and ravaged cities and towns; Yuan with six thousand foot and horse proclaimed a host of thirty thousand and advanced slowly.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Qiang of Jing Province rebelled and ravaged the towns; Yuan took six thousand foot and cavalry, proclaimed a host of thirty thousand, and advanced at an unhurried pace.

sentences.zh: 未經三旬，賊眾逃散，降者數萬口，唯梟首惡，餘悉不問。

translations.literal: Within less than thirty days the rebel host fled and scattered; those who surrendered numbered tens of thousands; only the chief evildoers were beheaded, the rest were not questioned at all.
translations.idiomatic: In less than thirty days the rebels fled and scattered; tens of thousands surrendered; only the ringleaders were executed, and the rest went unpunished.

sentences.zh: 詔兼侍中。

translations.literal: An edict appointed him concurrent Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed concurrent Palace Attendant by edict.

sentences.zh: 初，淵年十四，嘗詣長安。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Yuan was fourteen, he once went to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan was fourteen he once visited Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 將還，諸相餞送者五十餘人，別於渭北。

translations.literal: When he was about to return, more than fifty who had come to see him off took leave north of the Wei.
translations.idiomatic: As he was about to return, more than fifty friends who had come to see him off took their leave north of the Wei River.

sentences.zh: 有相者扶風人王伯達曰：「諸君皆不如此盧郎，雖位不副實，然德聲甚盛，望踰公輔。

translations.literal: A physiognomist, Wang Boda of Fufeng, said: "You gentlemen are none like this Master Lu; though his rank does not match his substance, yet his reputation for virtue is very great, and his prospects exceed those of the Three Excellencies."
translations.idiomatic: A physiognomist, Wang Boda of Fufeng, said: "None of you gentlemen is like this young Master Lu; though his rank does not yet match his worth, his reputation for virtue is already great, and his prospects surpass those of the highest ministers."

sentences.zh: 後二十餘年，當制命關右。

translations.literal: After twenty-odd years, you will hold commanding authority west of the Pass.
translations.idiomatic: In twenty-odd years you will hold command west of the Pass.

sentences.zh: 願不相忘。

translations.literal: I wish you will not forget me.
translations.idiomatic: Do not forget me.

sentences.zh: 」此行也，相者年過八十，詣軍門請見，言敍平生。

translations.literal: On this campaign the physiognomist had passed eighty; he came to the army gate to request an audience and spoke of recounting his life's course.
translations.idiomatic: On this expedition the physiognomist, now past eighty, came to the camp gate to request an audience and reminisced about their past acquaintance.

sentences.zh: 未幾，拜儀曹尚書。

translations.literal: Before long, he was appointed Minister of the Ceremonial Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was appointed Minister of the Ceremonial Bureau.

sentences.zh: 高祖考課在位，降淵以王師守常侍、尚書，奪常侍祿一周。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowen assessed officials in office; he demoted Yuan to Regular Attendant and Minister on the staff of the Master Instructor, and removed his Regular Attendant salary for one review cycle.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowen (Gaozu) evaluated incumbents, he demoted Yuan to Regular Attendant and Minister on the Master Instructor's staff and stripped one cycle of his Regular Attendant salary.

sentences.zh: 尋除豫州刺史，以母老固辭。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Governor of Yu Province, but firmly declined on grounds of his mother's age.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed Governor of Yu Province but firmly declined because his mother was elderly.

sentences.zh: 會蕭昭業雍州刺史曹虎遣使請降，乃以淵為使持節、安南將軍，督前鋒諸軍徑赴樊鄧。

translations.literal: When Cao Hu, Governor of Yong Province under Xiao Zhaoye, sent envoys offering surrender, Yuan was made Bearer of the Staff, General Who Pacifies the South, supervising the vanguard armies to proceed directly to Fan and Deng.
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Hu, Xiao Zhaoye's Governor of Yong Province, sent envoys offering surrender, Yuan was appointed Bearer of the Staff and General Who Pacifies the South to lead the vanguard straight to Fan and Deng.

sentences.zh: 淵面辭曰：「臣本儒生，頗聞俎豆，軍旅之事，未之學也。

translations.literal: Yuan declined in person, saying: "Your servant is originally a Confucian scholar; I am somewhat versed in ritual vessels; of military affairs I have not studied them."
translations.idiomatic: Yuan declined in person, saying: "I am a Confucian scholar by training, versed in ritual and ceremony; I have never studied the art of war."

sentences.zh: 惟陛下裁之。

translations.literal: I leave it solely to Your Majesty's decision.
translations.idiomatic: I leave the decision entirely to Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 」軍期已逼，高祖不許。

translations.literal: "] The army's departure date pressed close; Emperor Xiaowen did not consent.
translations.idiomatic: The army's departure date was imminent, and Emperor Xiaowen (Gaozu) would not allow it.

sentences.zh: 淵曰：「但恐曹虎為周魴耳，陛下宜審之。

translations.literal: Yuan said: "I only fear Cao Hu may be another Zhou Fang; Your Majesty should examine the matter carefully."
translations.idiomatic: Yuan said: "I fear only that Cao Hu may be another Zhou Fang; Your Majesty should look into this carefully."

sentences.zh: 」虎果偽降。

translations.literal: "] Hu indeed feigned surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Hu's surrender proved to be a ruse.

sentences.zh: 淵至葉，具曹虎譎詐之問，兼陳其利害。

translations.literal: When Yuan reached Ye, he fully reported Cao Hu's treacherous deceit and also set forth the advantages and disadvantages.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan reached Ye, he laid out Cao Hu's treachery in full and explained the strategic stakes.

sentences.zh: 詔淵進取南陽。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Yuan to advance and take Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Yuan to advance and capture Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 淵以兵少糧乏，表求先攻赭陽，以近葉倉故也。

translations.literal: Yuan, because troops were few and provisions scarce, memorialized requesting first to attack Zheyang, since it lay near Ye's granary.
translations.idiomatic: Because his forces were few and supplies short, Yuan memorialized asking to attack Zheyang first, since it was close to the granary at Ye.

sentences.zh: 高祖許焉，乃進攻赭陽。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowen consented, and they advanced to attack Zheyang.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen (Gaozu) agreed, and the army advanced on Zheyang.

sentences.zh: 蕭鸞遣將垣歷生來救，淵素無將略，為賊所敗，坐免官爵為民。

translations.literal: Xiao Luan sent General Yuan Lisheng to the rescue; Yuan had never possessed military stratagem and was defeated by the enemy; he was dismissed from office and rank and reduced to commoner status.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Luan sent General Yuan Lisheng to relieve the city; Yuan had never been skilled in command and was defeated; he was stripped of office and rank and reduced to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 尋遭母憂，高祖遣謁者詣宅宣慰。

translations.literal: Before long he encountered his mother's death; Emperor Xiaowen sent an envoy to his residence to proclaim consolation.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward his mother died; Emperor Xiaowen (Gaozu) sent an envoy to his home to offer condolences.

sentences.zh: 服闋，兼太尉長史。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, he served concurrently as Chief Clerk of the Grand Mentor.
translations.idiomatic: When his mourning period ended, he served concurrently as Chief Clerk to the Grand Mentor.

sentences.zh: 高祖南討，又兼彭城王中軍府長史。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowen campaigned south, he also served concurrently as Chief Clerk of the Prince of Pengcheng's Central Army Headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowen (Gaozu) marched south, he also served as Chief Clerk of the Prince of Pengcheng's central army headquarters.

sentences.zh: 尋為徐州、京兆王愉兼長史，賜絹百匹。

translations.literal: Soon he became concurrent Chief Clerk to the Prince of Xuzhou and Jingzhao, Yuan Yu, and was granted one hundred bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made concurrent chief clerk to Prince Yu of Xuzhou and Jingzhao and granted one hundred bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 愉既年少，事無巨細，多決於淵。

translations.literal: Since Yu was still young, whether matters were great or small, most decisions rested with Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: Yu was still young, and whether affairs were great or small, most decisions fell to Yuan.

sentences.zh: 淵以誠信御物，甚得東南民和。

translations.literal: Yuan governed people with sincerity and trust, and won the goodwill of the southeastern populace exceedingly.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan governed with sincerity and trust and won great goodwill among the people of the southeast.

sentences.zh: 南徐州刺史沈陵密謀外叛，淵覺其萌漸，潛敕諸戍，微為之備。

translations.literal: Shen Ling, Governor of Southern Xuzhou, secretly plotted defection abroad; Yuan perceived the first signs and secretly ordered the garrisons to make slight preparations.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Ling, Governor of Southern Xuzhou, secretly plotted to defect; Yuan detected the first signs and quietly ordered the garrisons to make discreet preparations.

sentences.zh: 屢有表聞，朝廷不納。

translations.literal: He repeatedly memorialized the court, but the court did not accept it.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized the court repeatedly, but the court paid no heed.

sentences.zh: 陵果殺將佐，勒宿豫之眾逃叛。

translations.literal: Ling indeed killed his staff officers and forced the garrison at Suqian to flee in rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Ling did kill his officers and drive the garrison at Suqian into flight and rebellion.

sentences.zh: 濱淮諸戍，由備得全。

translations.literal: The garrisons along the Huai River banks were preserved whole through these preparations.
translations.idiomatic: The garrisons along the Huai were preserved intact thanks to those preparations.

sentences.zh: 陵在邊歷年，陰結既廣，二州人情，咸相扇惑。

translations.literal: Ling had been on the frontier for years and his secret connections were already wide; the sentiments of the two provinces were all mutually incited and deluded.
translations.idiomatic: Ling had spent years on the frontier building secret ties, and sentiment in both provinces fed on one another's agitation.

sentences.zh: 陵之餘黨，頗見執送，淵皆撫而赦之，惟歸罪於陵，由是眾心乃安。

translations.literal: Ling's remaining partisans were largely captured and sent in; Yuan all comforted and pardoned them, assigning guilt only to Ling; thereby the people's hearts were reassured.
translations.idiomatic: Many of Ling's remaining followers were captured and sent in; Yuan comforted and pardoned them all, laying blame only on Ling, and so the people's minds were settled.

sentences.zh: 景明初，除祕書監。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jingming, he was appointed Superintendent of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Jingming era he was appointed Superintendent of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 二年卒官，年四十八。

translations.literal: In the second year he died in office, aged forty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he died in office, at the age of forty-eight.

sentences.zh: 贈安北將軍、幽州刺史，復本爵固安伯，諡曰懿。

translations.literal: Posthumously awarded General Who Pacifies the North and Governor of You Province, restored to his original title Marquis of Gu'an, posthumous name Yi.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made General Who Pacifies the North and Governor of You Province, restored to his original title Marquis of Gu'an, with the posthumous name Yi.

sentences.zh: 初，諶父志法鍾繇書，傳業累世，世有能名。

translations.literal: At first, Chen and his father took Zhong Yao's calligraphy as their model; the craft was handed down through generations, and each generation produced men of recognized skill.
translations.idiomatic: From the time of Chen and his father, the family took Zhong Yao's calligraphy as its model; the art passed down through generations, and each produced men of renown.

sentences.zh: 至邈以上，兼善草迹。

translations.literal: From Miao upward, they also excelled in cursive script.
translations.idiomatic: From Miao's generation onward they also excelled in cursive script.

sentences.zh: 淵習家法，代京宮殿多淵所題。

translations.literal: Yuan studied the family tradition; many palace buildings in the capital were inscribed by Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan mastered the family style, and many palace buildings in the capital bore his inscriptions.

sentences.zh: 白馬公崔玄伯亦善書，世傳衞瓘體。

translations.literal: The Duke of Baima, Cui Xuanbo, was also skilled at calligraphy; the world transmitted the style of Wei Guan.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke of Baima, Cui Xuanbo, was also a fine calligrapher; his style was said to follow that of Wei Guan.

sentences.zh: 魏初工書者，崔盧二門。

translations.literal: In early Wei, the masters of calligraphy were the two clans of Cui and Lu.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Wei, the leading calligraphers came from the Cui and Lu clans.

sentences.zh: 淵與僕射李沖特相友善。

translations.literal: Yuan and Vice Director Li Chong were especially friendly with each other.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan and Vice Director Li Chong were especially close friends.

sentences.zh: 沖重淵門風，而淵祗沖才官，故結為婚姻，往來親密。

translations.literal: Chong valued the Lu family's standing, and Yuan revered Chong's talent and office; therefore they formed a marriage alliance and were intimate in their coming and going.
translations.idiomatic: Chong respected the standing of the Lu house, and Yuan revered Chong's talent and rank; they therefore formed a marriage alliance and were intimate in their dealings.

sentences.zh: 至於淵荷高祖意遇，頗亦由沖。

translations.literal: Even Yuan's receiving Emperor Xiaowen's gracious favor owed much to Chong as well.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan's receiving Emperor Xiaowen's (Gaozu's) gracious favor owed much to Chong as well.

sentences.zh: 淵有八子。

translations.literal: Yuan had eight sons.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan had eight sons.

sentences.zh: 長子道將，字祖業，應襲父爵，而讓其第八弟道舒。

translations.literal: The eldest son Dao Jiang, style Zuye, was to inherit his father's enfeoffment, but yielded it to his eighth younger brother Dao Shu.
translations.idiomatic: The eldest son, Dao Jiang, style Zuye, was due to inherit his father's title but yielded it to his eighth brother, Dao Shu.

sentences.zh: 有司奏聞，詔曰：「長嫡承重，禮之大經，何得輒授也。

translations.literal: The authorities memorialized the matter; the edict said: "The eldest legitimate son bears the weight of the line — this is the great canon of ritual; how can he casually transfer it?"
translations.idiomatic: The authorities reported the matter, and an edict said: "The eldest legitimate son bears the weight of the line — that is the great principle of ritual; how can he simply give it away?"

sentences.zh: 」而道將引清河王國常侍韓子熙讓弟仲穆魯陽男之例，[2]尚書李平重申奏，詔乃聽許。

translations.literal: "] But Dao Jiang cited the precedent of Han Zixi, Regular Attendant of the Prince of Qinghe's kingdom, who yielded to his younger brother Zhongmu, Baron of Luyang,[2] and Minister Li Ping submitted again; the edict then permitted it.
translations.idiomatic: Dao Jiang cited the precedent of Han Zixi, Regular Attendant of the Prince of Qinghe's kingdom, who had yielded his title to his younger brother Zhongmu, Baron of Luyang,[2] and Minister Li Ping resubmitted the memorial; the edict then granted permission.

sentences.zh: 道將涉獵經史，風氣謇諤，頗有文才，為一家後來之冠，諸父並敬憚之。

translations.literal: Dao Jiang ranged through the classics and histories; his manner was forthright and blunt; he possessed considerable literary talent, the foremost of his generation in the family; his uncles all respected and feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Dao Jiang ranged widely in the classics and histories; his bearing was forthright and blunt; he had real literary talent and stood at the head of the younger generation in the family, and his uncles all respected and feared him.

sentences.zh: 彭城王勰、任城王澄皆虛襟相待。

translations.literal: The Prince of Pengcheng, Xie, and the Prince of Rencheng, Cheng, both received him with open modesty.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xie of Pengcheng and Prince Cheng of Rencheng both received him with open-hearted courtesy.

sentences.zh: 勰為中軍大將軍，辟行參軍。

translations.literal: When Xie was Grand General of the Central Army, he recruited him as Clerk in the General's Staff.
translations.idiomatic: When Xie served as Grand General of the Central Army, he recruited Dao Jiang as a clerk on his staff.

sentences.zh: 遷司徒東閤祭酒、尚書左外兵郎中，轉祕書丞。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Libationer of the Eastern Pavilion of the Minister of Works, Director of the Left Outer Troops Bureau in the Ministry of Works, and transferred to Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Libationer of the Eastern Pavilion under the Minister of Works, then Director of the Left Outer Troops Bureau, and later transferred to Secretary.

sentences.zh: 出為燕郡太守。

translations.literal: He was sent out as Administrator of Yan Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out to serve as Administrator of Yan Commandery.

sentences.zh: 道將下車，表樂毅、霍原之墓，而為之立祠。

translations.literal: When Dao Jiang took up his post, he memorialized the tombs of Yue Yi and Huo Yuan and had shrines erected for them.
translations.idiomatic: Upon taking office, Dao Jiang memorialized the tombs of Yue Yi and Huo Yuan and had shrines built for them.

sentences.zh: 優禮儒生，勵勸學業，敦課農桑，墾田歲倍。

translations.literal: He honored Confucian scholars, urged on their studies, pressed the cultivation of mulberry and grain, and opened new fields until the farmland doubled within the year.
translations.idiomatic: He honored Confucian scholars, encouraged learning, pressed agriculture and sericulture, and opened new fields until the acreage under cultivation doubled within a year.

sentences.zh: 入為司徒司馬。

translations.literal: He was recalled to serve as Marshal of the Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to serve as Marshal under the Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈龍驤將軍、太常少卿，諡曰獻。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously awarded General of Majestic Cavalry and Vice Minister of Ceremonies, posthumous name Xian.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made General of Majestic Cavalry and Vice Minister of Ceremonies, with the posthumous name Xian.

sentences.zh: 所為文筆數十篇。

translations.literal: Writings he composed numbered several tens of pieces.
translations.idiomatic: He left several dozen pieces of writing.

sentences.zh: 子懷祖，太學博士、員外散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: His son Huai Zu was Doctor of the Imperial University and Supernumerary Gentleman Attendant at Large.
translations.idiomatic: His son Huai Zu served as Doctor of the Imperial University and Supernumerary Gentleman Attendant at Large.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 懷祖弟懷仁，武定中，太尉鎧曹參軍。

translations.literal: Huai Zu's younger brother Huai Ren, during Wuding, served as Armor Bureau Clerk on the Grand Mentor's staff.
translations.idiomatic: Huai Zu's younger brother Huai Ren, during the Wuding era, served as Armor Bureau Clerk on the Grand Mentor's staff.

sentences.zh: 道將弟亮，字仁業。

translations.literal: Dao Jiang's younger brother Liang, style Renye.
translations.idiomatic: Dao Jiang's younger brother Liang, style Renye.

sentences.zh: [3]不仕而終。

translations.literal: [3] He did not take office and died.
translations.idiomatic: [3] He never took office and died.

sentences.zh: 子思道。

translations.literal: His son was Sidao.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Sidao.

sentences.zh: 亮弟道裕，字寧祖，少以學尚知名，風儀兼美。

translations.literal: Liang's younger brother Dao Yu, style Ningzu, from youth was known for scholarly attainments; his bearing and deportment were both fine.
translations.idiomatic: Liang's younger brother Dao Yu, style Ningzu, was known from youth for his learning, and his bearing and deportment were both fine.

sentences.zh: 尚顯祖女樂浪長公主，拜駙馬都尉、太子舍人，尋轉洗馬。

translations.literal: He married the Princess of Lelang, daughter of Emperor Xianzu, and was appointed Chief Commandant of the Imperial Son-in-Law and Attendant of the Heir Apparent; soon he was transferred to Groom of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He married the Princess of Lelang, daughter of Emperor Xianzu, and was appointed Chief Commandant of the Imperial Son-in-Law and Attendant of the Heir Apparent; he was soon transferred to Groom of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 遷散騎侍郎，轉安遠將軍、中書侍郎、兼祕書丞。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Gentleman Attendant at Large, transferred to General of Distant Pacification, Palace Attendant of the Secretariat, and concurrent Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Gentleman Attendant at Large, then made General of Distant Pacification, Palace Attendant of the Secretariat, and concurrent Secretary.

sentences.zh: 尋以母憂去官。

translations.literal: Soon, on account of his mother's death, he left office.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he left office upon his mother's death.

sentences.zh: 服終，復拜中書侍郎。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, he was again appointed Palace Attendant of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When his mourning ended, he was again appointed Palace Attendant of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 遷龍驤將軍、太子中庶子，幽州大中正。

translations.literal: He was promoted to General of Majestic Cavalry, Senior Tutor of the Heir Apparent, and Chief Arbiter of You Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to General of Majestic Cavalry, Senior Tutor of the Heir Apparent, and Chief Arbiter of You Province.

sentences.zh: 轉長兼散騎侍郎，加左將軍。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Senior concurrent Gentleman Attendant at Large, with the additional title General of the Left.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Senior concurrent Gentleman Attendant at Large and given the additional title General of the Left.

sentences.zh: 神龜二年，除左將軍、涇州刺史。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shengui, he was appointed General of the Left and Governor of Jing Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Shengui he was appointed General of the Left and Governor of Jing Province.

sentences.zh: 其年七月卒官，年四十四。

translations.literal: That year in the seventh month he died in office, aged forty-four.
translations.idiomatic: That same year, in the seventh month, he died in office at the age of forty-four.

sentences.zh: 贈撫軍將軍、青州刺史，賜帛三百匹，諡曰文侯。

translations.literal: Posthumously awarded General Who Pacifies the Army and Governor of Qing Province, granted three hundred bolts of silk, posthumous title Marquis Wen.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made General Who Pacifies the Army and Governor of Qing Province, granted three hundred bolts of silk, and given the posthumous title Marquis Wen.

sentences.zh: 子景緒，武定中，儀同開府錄事參軍。

translations.literal: His son Jingxu, during Wuding, served as Record-keeping Clerk of the Office Equal in Rank to the Prefect of Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jingxu, during the Wuding era, served as record-keeping clerk in an office equal in rank to the prefect of affairs.

sentences.zh: 道裕弟道虔，字慶祖，粗閑經史，兼通算術。

translations.literal: Dao Yu's younger brother Dao Qian, style Qingzu, was roughly versed in classics and histories and also understood arithmetic.
translations.idiomatic: Dao Yu's younger brother Dao Qian, style Qingzu, had a working knowledge of the classics and histories and was also versed in arithmetic.

sentences.zh: 尚高祖女濟南長公主。

translations.literal: He married the Princess of Jinan, daughter of Emperor Xiaowen.
translations.idiomatic: He married the Princess of Jinan, daughter of Emperor Xiaowen (Gaozu).

sentences.zh: 公主驕淫，聲穢遐邇，先無疹患，倉卒暴薨。

translations.literal: The princess was arrogant and licentious; her scandalous repute spread far and near; previously she had no illness, yet she suddenly died violently.
translations.idiomatic: The princess was arrogant and licentious, and her scandalous reputation spread far and wide; she had shown no sign of illness, yet she died suddenly and violently.

sentences.zh: 時云道虔所害。

translations.literal: At the time people said Dao Qian had killed her.
translations.idiomatic: At the time people said Dao Qian had killed her.

sentences.zh: 世宗祕其醜惡，不苦窮治。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanwu concealed her disgrace and did not press the investigation harshly.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanwu kept her disgrace secret and did not pursue the case to the full.

sentences.zh: 尚書嘗奏道虔為國子博士。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Works once memorialized appointing Dao Qian as Doctor of the Imperial University.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Works once memorialized appointing Dao Qian as Doctor of the Imperial University.

sentences.zh: 靈太后追主薨事，乃黜道虔為民，終身不仕。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Ling pursued the matter of the princess's death and demoted Dao Qian to commoner status, forbidding him from holding office for life.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Ling reopened the investigation into the princess's death, demoted Dao Qian to commoner status, and barred him from office for life.

sentences.zh: 孝昌末。

translations.literal: At the end of the Xiaochang era.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Xiaochang era.

sentences.zh: 臨淮王彧因將出征，啟除道虔奉車都尉。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Linhuai, Yu, was about to lead troops on campaign, he petitioned to appoint Dao Qian Chief Commandant of the Imperial Carriage.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Yu of Linhuai was about to take the field, he petitioned to appoint Dao Qian Chief Commandant of the Imperial Carriage.

sentences.zh: 道虔外生李彧尚莊帝姊豐亭公主，因相藉託。

translations.literal: Dao Qian's maternal nephew Li Yu had married the Princess of Fengting, sister of Emperor Zhuang; through this connection they relied on each other.
translations.idiomatic: Dao Qian's maternal nephew Li Yu had married the Princess of Fengting, sister of Emperor Zhuang, and through that connection they relied on one another.

sentences.zh: 永安中，除輔國將軍、通直常侍，尋加征虜將軍。

translations.literal: During the Yong'an era, he was appointed General Who Assists the State and Regular Attendant of Direct Communication; soon he was additionally made General Who Captures the Enemy.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yong'an era he was appointed General Who Assists the State and Regular Attendant of Direct Communication, and soon afterward was additionally made General Who Captures the Enemy.

sentences.zh: 以議曆勳，賜爵臨淄伯，遷散騎常侍。

translations.literal: For his merit in calendar reform, he was enfeoffed as Baron of Linzi and promoted to Regular Attendant at Large.
translations.idiomatic: For his service in calendar reform he was enfeoffed as Baron of Linzi and promoted to Regular Attendant at Large.

sentences.zh: 天平初，征南將軍，轉都官尚書、本州大中正。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianping, he was General Who Subdues the South; he was transferred to Minister of Justice and Chief Arbiter of his home province.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Tianping era he was made General Who Subdues the South, then transferred to Minister of Justice and Chief Arbiter of his home province.

sentences.zh: 出除驃騎將軍、幽州刺史，尋加衞大將軍，卒於官。

translations.literal: He was sent out and dismissed as General of Fast Cavalry and Governor of You Province; soon he was additionally made Grand General of the Guard; he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as General of Fast Cavalry and Governor of You Province, soon given the additional title Grand General of the Guard, and died in office.

sentences.zh: 贈都督幽瀛二州諸軍事、驃騎大將軍、尚書右僕射、司空公、瀛州刺史，諡曰恭文公。

translations.literal: Posthumously awarded Supervisor of All Military Affairs of You and Ying Provinces, General of Fast Cavalry, Right Vice Director of the Ministry of Works, Duke of the Ministry of Works, Governor of Ying Province, posthumous name Duke Gongwen.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Supervisor of All Military Affairs of You and Ying Provinces, General of Fast Cavalry, Right Vice Director of the Ministry of Works, Duke of the Ministry of Works, and Governor of Ying Province, with the posthumous title Duke Gongwen.

sentences.zh: 主二子，昌宇、昌仁。

translations.literal: He had two sons, Changyu and Changren.
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons, Changyu and Changren.

sentences.zh: 昌宇不慧，昌仁早卒。

translations.literal: Changyu was dull-witted; Changren died young.
translations.idiomatic: Changyu was dull-witted, and Changren died young.

sentences.zh: 道虔又娶司馬氏，有子昌裕。

translations.literal: Dao Qian also married a Lady Sima and had a son Changyu.
translations.idiomatic: Dao Qian also married a Lady of the Sima clan and had a son, Changyu.

sentences.zh: 及司馬見出之後，更娉元氏，生二子昌期、昌衡。

translations.literal: After Lady Sima was divorced, he took Lady Yuan in marriage again and bore two sons, Changqi and Changheng.
translations.idiomatic: After Lady Sima was divorced, he married again into the Yuan clan and had two sons, Changqi and Changheng.

sentences.zh: 兄弟競父爵，至今未襲。

translations.literal: The brothers contended over their father's enfeoffment; to this day it had not been inherited.
translations.idiomatic: The brothers contested their father's title, and to this day it had still not been inherited.

sentences.zh: 道虔弟道侃，字希祖。

translations.literal: Dao Qian's younger brother Dao Kan, style Xizu.
translations.idiomatic: Dao Qian's younger brother Dao Kan, style Xizu.

sentences.zh: 州主簿，沉雅有學尚。

translations.literal: Provincial secretariat clerk; refined and possessed scholarly attainments.
translations.idiomatic: He served as provincial secretariat clerk; he was refined and scholarly.

sentences.zh: 孝昌末卒。

translations.literal: He died at the end of the Xiaochang era.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the end of the Xiaochang era.

sentences.zh: 二子早夭，以弟道約子正達為後。

translations.literal: His two sons died young; he took his younger brother Dao Yue's son Zhengda as heir.
translations.idiomatic: His two sons died young, and he took his younger brother Dao Yue's son Zhengda as his heir.

sentences.zh: 武定中，征虜將軍、太尉記室參軍。

translations.literal: During Wuding, General Who Captures the Enemy and Recording Clerk on the Grand Mentor's staff.
translations.idiomatic: During the Wuding era he served as General Who Captures the Enemy and recording clerk on the Grand Mentor's staff.

sentences.zh: 道侃弟道和，字叔維。

translations.literal: Dao Kan's younger brother Dao He, style Shuwei.
translations.idiomatic: Dao Kan's younger brother Dao He, style Shuwei.

sentences.zh: [4]兄弟之中，人望最下。

translations.literal: [4] Among the brothers, his public esteem was the lowest.
translations.idiomatic: [4] Among the brothers, he ranked lowest in public esteem.

sentences.zh: 冀州中軍府中兵參軍。

translations.literal: Middle Army Clerk of the Central Army Headquarters of Ji Province.
translations.idiomatic: He served as middle army clerk in the central army headquarters of Ji Province.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 子景豫。

translations.literal: His son was Jingyu.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Jingyu.

sentences.zh: 景豫弟景熙，武定中，儀同開府諮議。

translations.literal: Jingyu's younger brother Jingxi, during Wuding, served as staff adviser of an office equal in rank to the prefect of affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Jingyu's younger brother Jingxi, during the Wuding era, served as staff adviser in an office equal in rank to the prefect of affairs.

sentences.zh: 道和弟道約，字季恭。

translations.literal: Dao He's younger brother Dao Yue, style Jigong.
translations.idiomatic: Dao He's younger brother Dao Yue, style Jigong.

sentences.zh: 起家員外郎，累遷司空錄事參軍、司徒屬、幽州大中正、輔國將軍、光祿大夫。

translations.literal: He entered office as Cadet Gentleman and was successively promoted to Record-keeping Clerk under the Minister of Works, Staff Member of the Grand Mentor, Chief Arbiter of You Province, General Who Assists the State, and Household Grandee of the Imperial Household.
translations.idiomatic: He began his career as Cadet Gentleman and was successively promoted to record-keeping clerk under the Minister of Works, staff member of the Grand Mentor, Chief Arbiter of You Province, General Who Assists the State, and Household Grandee of the Imperial Household.

sentences.zh: 轉司徒右長史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Right Senior Clerk of the Grand Mentor.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Right Senior Clerk of the Grand Mentor.

sentences.zh: 太傅李延寔出除青州。

translations.literal: Grand Preceptor Li Yanshi was sent out and appointed to Qing Province.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Preceptor Li Yanshi was sent out to take up the governorship of Qing Province.

sentences.zh: 延寔先被病，道約，延寔之妻弟，詔以道約為延寔長史，加散騎常侍，寄以匡維也。

translations.literal: Yanshi had already fallen ill; Dao Yue, Yanshi's brother-in-law, was by edict made Yanshi's chief clerk, with the additional title Regular Attendant at Large, entrusted with support and guidance.
translations.idiomatic: Yanshi was already ill; Dao Yue, his brother-in-law, was appointed by edict as Yanshi's chief clerk with the additional title Regular Attendant at Large, entrusted to support and guide him.

sentences.zh: 永熙中，車騎將軍、左光祿大夫，領廣平王贊儀同開府長史。

translations.literal: During Yongxi, General of Chariots and Cavalry and Left Household Grandee of the Imperial Household, concurrently chief clerk of the office equal in rank to the prefect of affairs held by Prince Zan of Guangping.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yongxi era he served as General of Chariots and Cavalry and Left Household Grandee of the Imperial Household, and concurrently as chief clerk in the office equal in rank to the prefect of affairs held by Prince Zan of Guangping.

sentences.zh: 天平中，開府儀同高岳請為長史。

translations.literal: During Tianping, Gao Yue, whose office was equal in rank to the prefect of affairs, requested him as chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianping era Gao Yue, whose office was equal in rank to the prefect of affairs, asked him to serve as chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 岳轉除青冀二州，道約仍為長史，隨岳兩藩，有毗佐之稱。

translations.literal: When Yue was transferred to govern Qing and Ji Provinces, Dao Yue remained chief clerk; following Yue through both governorships, he won renown as an effective aide.
translations.idiomatic: When Yue was transferred to govern Qing and Ji Provinces, Dao Yue remained his chief clerk; accompanying Yue through both postings, he earned a reputation as an able assistant.

sentences.zh: 興和末，除衞大將軍、兗州刺史，在州頗得民和。

translations.literal: At the end of Xinghe, he was appointed Grand General of the Guard and Governor of Yan Province; in office he kept the people well reconciled.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Xinghe era he was appointed Grand General of the Guard and Governor of Yan Province, where he kept the people on good terms with the government.

sentences.zh: 武定元年卒，年五十八。

translations.literal: He died in the first year of Wuding, aged fifty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the first year of Wuding, at the age of fifty-eight.

sentences.zh: 贈使持節、驃騎大將軍、儀同三司、幽州刺史。

translations.literal: Posthumously awarded Bearer of the Staff, General of Fast Cavalry, Office Equal in Rank to the Three Excellencies, and Governor of You Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Bearer of the Staff, General of Fast Cavalry, an office equal in rank to the Three Excellencies, and Governor of You Province.

sentences.zh: 子正通，開府諮議。

translations.literal: His son Zhengtong, staff adviser of an opening office.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhengtong served as staff adviser in an opening office.

sentences.zh: 少有令譽，徵赴晉陽，遇患卒。

translations.literal: In youth he had a fine reputation; summoned to Jinyang, he fell ill on the way and died.
translations.idiomatic: He had a fine reputation in youth; summoned to Jinyang, he fell ill en route and died.

sentences.zh: 妻鄭氏，與正通弟正思淫亂，武定中，為御史所劾，人士疾之。

translations.literal: His wife, née Zheng, carried on an illicit affair with Zhengtong's younger brother Zhengsi; during Wuding she was impeached by the censorate, and scholars despised them.
translations.idiomatic: His wife, Lady Zheng, had an affair with Zhengtong's younger brother Zhengsi; during the Wuding era the censorate impeached them, and men of standing reviled the affair.

sentences.zh: 道約弟道舒，字幼安，襲父爵。

translations.literal: Dao Yue's younger brother Dao Shu, style You'an, inherited his father's title.
translations.idiomatic: Dao Yue's younger brother Dao Shu, style You'an, inherited his father's title.

sentences.zh: 自尚書左主客郎中為冠軍將軍、中書侍郎。

translations.literal: From Chief of the Left Foreign Guests Bureau in the Ministry of State Affairs he became General Who Wins Battles and Attendant Gentleman of the Central Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He rose from Chief of the Left Foreign Guests Bureau in the Ministry of State Affairs to General Who Wins Battles and Attendant Gentleman of the Central Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 淵弟敏，字仲通，小字紅崖，少有大量。

translations.literal: Yuan's younger brother Min, style Zhongtong, childhood name Hongya, from youth possessed broad capacity.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan's younger brother Min, style Zhongtong, called Hongya as a child, had a generous nature from youth.

sentences.zh: 太和初，拜議郎，早卒。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taihe, he was appointed Gentleman Adviser; he died young.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Taihe era he was appointed Gentleman Adviser, but died young.

sentences.zh: 贈威遠將軍、范陽太守，諡曰靖。

translations.literal: Posthumously awarded General Who Shows Power From Afar and Governor of Fanyang; posthumous title Jing.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made General Who Shows Power From Afar and Governor of Fanyang, with the posthumous title Jing.

sentences.zh: 高祖納其女為嬪。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowen took his daughter as an imperial consort.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen (Gaozu) took his daughter as an imperial consort.

sentences.zh: 敏五子。

translations.literal: Min had five sons.
translations.idiomatic: Min had five sons.

sentences.zh: 義僖，字遠慶，早有學尚，識度沉雅。

translations.literal: Yixi, style Yuanqing, early possessed scholarly attainments; in judgment and bearing he was calm and refined.
translations.idiomatic: Yixi, style Yuanqing, was scholarly from an early age, with a calm and refined mind.

sentences.zh: 年九歲，喪父，便有至性。

translations.literal: At nine years he lost his father and already showed utmost filial nature.
translations.idiomatic: When he was nine he lost his father and already showed the deepest filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 少為僕射李沖所歎美。

translations.literal: In youth he was praised and admired by Vice Director Li Chong.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he won the admiration of Vice Director Li Chong.

sentences.zh: 起家祕書郎，歷太子舍人、司徒中郎。

translations.literal: He entered office as Secretariat Gentleman and served as Crown Prince Household Attendant and Staff Gentleman under the Grand Mentor.
translations.idiomatic: He began his career as Secretariat Gentleman and served as Crown Prince Household Attendant and staff gentleman under the Grand Mentor.

sentences.zh: 神龜初，任城王澄奏舉義僖，除散騎侍郎，轉冠軍將軍、中散大夫。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shengui, Prince Cheng of Rencheng memorialized recommending Yixi; he was appointed Attendant Gentleman at Large and transferred to General Who Wins Battles and Grand Master of Palace Service.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Shengui era Prince Cheng of Rencheng recommended Yixi; he was appointed Attendant Gentleman at Large, then transferred to General Who Wins Battles and Grand Master of Palace Service.

sentences.zh: 以母憂去職。

translations.literal: On account of mourning for his mother he left office.
translations.idiomatic: He resigned on account of mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 幽州刺史王誦與義僖交款，每與舊故李神儁等書曰：「盧冠軍在此，時復惠好，[5]輒留連數日，得諮詢政道。

translations.literal: Wang Song, Governor of You Province, was on intimate terms with Yixi; in letters to old friends such as Li Shenjun he would write: "General Lu is here; from time to time he shows me kindness, [5] and I often keep him for several days, able to consult him on the way of governance.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Song, Governor of You Province, was on close terms with Yixi; in letters to old friends such as Li Shenjun he wrote: "General Lu is here, and from time to time shows me kindness; [5] I often keep him for days on end and am able to consult him on affairs of state.

sentences.zh: 」其見重若此。

translations.literal: "] Such was the esteem in which he was held.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the esteem in which he was held.

sentences.zh: 齊王蕭寶夤啟為開府諮議參軍，辭疾不赴。

translations.literal: The Prince of Qi, Xiao Baoyin, petitioned to appoint him Staff Adviser of an opening office, but he declined on grounds of illness and did not take up the post.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xiao Baoyin of Qi petitioned to appoint him staff adviser in an opening office, but he declined on grounds of illness and did not go.

sentences.zh: 尋兼司空長史，拜征虜將軍、太中大夫。

translations.literal: Soon he was made concurrent Chief Clerk under the Minister of Works and appointed General Who Captures the Enemy and Grand Master of Palace Counselling.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made concurrent chief clerk under the Minister of Works and appointed General Who Captures the Enemy and Grand Master of Palace Counselling.

sentences.zh: 散秩多年，澹然自得。

translations.literal: For many years he held unoccupied rank, tranquil and self-content.
translations.idiomatic: For many years he held rank without active appointment, yet remained tranquil and at ease.

sentences.zh: 李神儁勸其干謁當途。

translations.literal: Li Shenjun urged him to pay court to those in power.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shenjun urged him to cultivate those then in power.

sentences.zh: 義僖曰：「學先王之道，貴行先王之志，何能苟求富貴也。」

translations.literal: Yixi said: "One studies the way of the former kings and values acting the will of the former kings—how could one seek wealth and rank opportunistically?"
translations.idiomatic: Yixi said: "One studies the way of the former kings and values living by their will—how could one grub after wealth and rank?"

sentences.zh: 孝昌中，除散騎常侍。

translations.literal: During Xiaochang, he was appointed Regular Attendant at Large.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xiaochang era he was appointed Regular Attendant at Large.

sentences.zh: 時靈太后臨朝，黃門侍郎李神軌勢傾朝野，求結婚姻。

translations.literal: At that time Empress Dowager Ling held court; Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate Li Shengui's power dominated court and countryside, and he sought a marriage alliance.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Empress Dowager Ling held court; Li Shengui, Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate, dominated court and countryside, and sought a marriage alliance with Yixi's family.

sentences.zh: 義僖慮其必敗，拒而不許。

translations.literal: Yixi feared he was bound to fall and refused, not consenting.
translations.idiomatic: Yixi feared Shengui was bound to fall and refused.

sentences.zh: 王誦謂義僖曰：「昔人不以一女易五男，卿豈易之也？

translations.literal: Wang Song said to Yixi: "People of old would not trade one daughter for five sons—would you make such a trade?
translations.idiomatic: Wang Song said to Yixi: "People of old would not trade one daughter for five sons—would you make such a bargain?

sentences.zh: 」義僖曰：「所以不從，正為此耳。

translations.literal: "] Yixi said: "The reason I do not consent is precisely this.
translations.idiomatic: Yixi said: "That is precisely why I refuse.

sentences.zh: 從之恐禍大而速。

translations.literal: If I consented, I fear disaster would come large and swift.
translations.idiomatic: If I agreed, I fear disaster would come swiftly and on a great scale.

sentences.zh: 」誦乃堅握義僖之手曰：「我聞有命，不敢以告人。

translations.literal: "] Song then firmly grasped Yixi's hand and said: "I have heard something I dare not tell others.
translations.idiomatic: Song then firmly grasped Yixi's hand and said: "I have heard something I dare not repeat to anyone.

sentences.zh: 」遂適他族。

translations.literal: "] She then married into another clan.
translations.idiomatic: She then married into another clan.

sentences.zh: 臨婚之夕，靈太后遣中常侍服景就家敕停。

translations.literal: On the eve of the wedding, Empress Dowager Ling sent Palace Attendant Fu Jing to the family home with an edict to halt it.
translations.idiomatic: On the eve of the wedding Empress Dowager Ling sent the eunuch Fu Jing to the family home with an edict stopping the marriage.

sentences.zh: 內外惶怖，義僖夷然自若。

translations.literal: Inside and outside the household were terrified; Yixi remained calm and unperturbed.
translations.idiomatic: The household was thrown into terror, but Yixi remained perfectly calm.

sentences.zh: 建義初，兼都官尚書，尋除安東將軍、衞尉卿。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianyi, he was made concurrent Minister of Punishments; soon he was appointed General Who Pacifies the East and Commandant of the Guard.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Jianyi era he was made concurrent Minister of Punishments, and soon afterward was appointed General Who Pacifies the East and Commandant of the Guard.

sentences.zh: 普泰中，除都官尚書，加驃騎大將軍、左光祿大夫。

translations.literal: During Putai, he was appointed Minister of Punishments, with the additional titles General of Fast Cavalry and Left Household Grandee of the Imperial Household.
translations.idiomatic: During the Putai era he was appointed Minister of Punishments, with the additional titles General of Fast Cavalry and Left Household Grandee of the Imperial Household.

sentences.zh: 義僖少時，幽州頻遭水旱，先有穀數萬石貸民，義僖以年穀不熟，乃燔其契。

translations.literal: When Yixi was young, You Province suffered repeated floods and droughts; he had previously lent the people tens of thousands of shi of grain; because the year's harvest was poor, Yixi burned the contracts.
translations.idiomatic: When Yixi was young, You Province suffered repeated floods and droughts; he had lent the people tens of thousands of shi of grain, and when the harvest failed he burned the loan contracts.

sentences.zh: 州閭悅其恩德。

translations.literal: The province and its neighborhoods rejoiced in his kindness and virtue.
translations.idiomatic: The people of the province rejoiced in his kindness.

sentences.zh: 性寬和畏慎，不妄交款，與魏子建情好尤篤，言無所隱。

translations.literal: By nature he was gentle, cautious, and reverent; he did not rashly form intimacies; his friendship with Wei Zijian was especially deep, and in speech he concealed nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Gentle, cautious, and reserved by nature, he did not form intimacies lightly; his friendship with Wei Zijian was especially close, and between them nothing was hidden.

sentences.zh: 義僖性清儉，不營財利，雖居顯位，每至困乏，麥飯蔬食，忻然甘之。

translations.literal: Yixi was by nature pure and frugal and did not pursue profit; though he held eminent rank, he often came to want, yet ate wheat and vegetables with willing pleasure.
translations.idiomatic: Yixi was pure and frugal by nature and did not pursue profit; though he held high office he often lived in want, yet ate plain wheat and vegetables with willing pleasure.

sentences.zh: 永熙中，風疾頓發。

translations.literal: During Yongxi, wind illness suddenly flared.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yongxi era he was suddenly stricken with wind paralysis.

sentences.zh: 興和中卒，年六十四。

translations.literal: He died during Xinghe, aged sixty-four.
translations.idiomatic: He died during the Xinghe era, at the age of sixty-four.

sentences.zh: 贈本將軍、儀同三司、瀛州刺史，諡孝簡。

translations.literal: Posthumously awarded his former generalship, Office Equal in Rank to the Three Excellencies, and Governor of Ying Province; posthumous title Xiao Jian.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted his former generalship, an office equal in rank to the Three Excellencies, and the governorship of Ying Province, with the posthumous title Xiao Jian.

sentences.zh: 子遜之，武定中，太尉記室參軍。

translations.literal: His son Xunzhi, during Wuding, served as Recording Clerk on the Grand Mentor's staff.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xunzhi, during the Wuding era, served as recording clerk on the Grand Mentor's staff.

sentences.zh: 遜之弟世猷，齊王開府集曹參軍。

translations.literal: Xunzhi's younger brother Shiyou, Staff Clerk of the Collecting Bureau in the Prince of Qi's opening office.
translations.idiomatic: Xunzhi's younger brother Shiyou served as staff clerk of the Collecting Bureau in the Prince of Qi's opening office.

sentences.zh: 義僖弟義悰，字叔預。

translations.literal: Yixi's younger brother Yicong, style Shuyu.
translations.idiomatic: Yixi's younger brother Yicong, style Shuyu.

sentences.zh: 司空行參軍、本州治中、散騎侍郎、司徒諮議參軍。

translations.literal: Acting Clerk under the Minister of Works, Provincial Administrator of his home province, Attendant Gentleman at Large, and Staff Adviser under the Grand Mentor.
translations.idiomatic: He served as acting clerk under the Minister of Works, provincial administrator of his home province, Attendant Gentleman at Large, and staff adviser under the Grand Mentor.

sentences.zh: 子孝章，儀同開府行參軍，早亡。

translations.literal: His son Xiaozhang, acting clerk in an office equal in rank to the prefect of affairs, died young.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xiaozhang, acting clerk in an office equal in rank to the prefect of affairs, died young.

sentences.zh: 義悰弟義敦，字季和。

translations.literal: Yicong's younger brother Yidun, style Jihe.
translations.idiomatic: Yicong's younger brother Yidun, style Jihe.

sentences.zh: 征北府默曹參軍。

translations.literal: Staff Clerk of the Silent Bureau in the Northern Expedition headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: He served as staff clerk of the Silent Bureau in the Northern Expedition headquarters.

sentences.zh: 子景開，字子達。

translations.literal: His son Jingkai, style Zida.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jingkai, style Zida.

sentences.zh: 武定中，儀同開府屬。

translations.literal: During Wuding, staff member of an office equal in rank to the prefect of affairs.
translations.idiomatic: During the Wuding era he served as staff member in an office equal in rank to the prefect of affairs.

sentences.zh: 義敦弟義安，字幼仁，不仕。

translations.literal: Yidun's younger brother Yian, style Youren, did not take office.
translations.idiomatic: Yidun's younger brother Yian, style Youren, never took office.

sentences.zh: 義僖諸弟並遠不逮兄也。

translations.literal: Yixi's various younger brothers all fell far short of their elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: All of Yixi's younger brothers fell far short of their elder brother.

sentences.zh: 敏弟昶，字叔達，小字師顏，學涉經史，早有時譽。

translations.literal: Min's younger brother Chang, style Shuda, childhood name Shiyan, erudite in the classics and histories, early possessed contemporary renown.
translations.idiomatic: Min's younger brother Chang, style Shuda, called Shiyan as a child, was versed in the classics and histories and had won early renown.

sentences.zh: 太和初，為太子中舍人、兼員外散騎常侍，使於蕭昭業。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taihe, he served as Crown Prince Household Attendant and concurrent Attendant Gentleman at Large for Foreign Affairs, envoy to Xiao Zhaoye.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Taihe era he served as Crown Prince Household Attendant and concurrent Attendant Gentleman at Large for Foreign Affairs on a mission to Xiao Zhaoye.
