sentences.zh: 高祖詔昶曰：「卿便至彼，勿存彼我。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowen edicted to Chang: "When you arrive there, do not preserve 'them and us.'
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen (Gaozu) instructed Chang: "When you arrive there, do not think in terms of 'them and us.'

sentences.zh: 密邇江揚，不早當晚，會是朕物。

translations.literal: Close to the Jiang and Yang regions—sooner or later, not early or late—it will in the end be my possession.
translations.idiomatic: The lands along the Yangzi are close at hand; sooner or later, not early or late, they will be mine in the end.

sentences.zh: 卿等欲言，便無相疑難。

translations.literal: If you wish to speak, then speak without mutual suspicion and difficulty.
translations.idiomatic: If you wish to speak, speak openly and without mutual suspicion.

sentences.zh: 」又敕副使王清石曰：「卿莫以本是南人，言語致慮。

translations.literal: "] He also edicted to the deputy envoy Wang Qingshi: "Do not, because you are originally a Southerner, let speech cause concern.
translations.idiomatic: He also instructed the deputy envoy Wang Qingshi: "Do not, because you are a Southerner by origin, let that make you hesitant in speech.

sentences.zh: 若彼先有所知所識，欲見便見，須論即論。

translations.literal: If they already know or recognize someone and wish to meet, then meet; if discussion is needed, then discuss.
translations.idiomatic: If they already know someone there and wish to meet him, meet him; if something must be discussed, discuss it.

sentences.zh: 盧昶正是寬柔君子，無多文才，或主客命卿作詩，可率卿所知，莫以昶不作，便復罷也。

translations.literal: Lu Chang is truly a gentle and yielding gentleman, without much literary talent; if host and guest should ask you to compose a poem, you may follow what you know—do not because Chang will not write, then stop altogether.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Chang is a gentle and yielding gentleman without much literary talent; if the hosts ask you to compose a poem, compose what you can—do not let the fact that Chang will not write stop you altogether.

sentences.zh: 凡使人之體，以和為貴，勿遞相矜誇，見於色貌，失將命之體。

translations.literal: The deportment of envoys generally values harmony; do not in succession vaunt and boast before one another, showing it in countenance and bearing, losing the proper body of bearing the mandate.
translations.idiomatic: The deportment of envoys should above all value harmony; do not take turns vaunting yourselves before one another in face and bearing, for that loses the dignity of bearing the imperial mandate.

sentences.zh: 卿等各率所知，以相規誨。

translations.literal: Each of you follow what you know, to mutually advise and instruct.
translations.idiomatic: Each of you should act according to your own strengths and counsel one another.

sentences.zh: 」及昶至彼，值蕭鸞僭立，於是高祖南討之，昶兄淵為別道將。

translations.literal: "] When Chang arrived there, it happened that Xiao Luan had usurped the throne; thereupon Emperor Xiaowen campaigned south against him, and Chang's elder brother Yuan was a general on a separate route.
translations.idiomatic: When Chang arrived, Xiao Luan had just usurped the throne; Emperor Xiaowen (Gaozu) then marched south against him, and Chang's elder brother Yuan served as a general on a separate route.

sentences.zh: 而蕭鸞以朝廷加兵，遂酷遇昶等。

translations.literal: And because Xiao Luan, on account of the court's dispatch of troops, then treated Chang and the others harshly.
translations.idiomatic: Because the Northern Wei court had sent troops, Xiao Luan treated Chang and his party with deliberate cruelty.

sentences.zh: 昶本非骨鯁，聞南人云兄既作將，弟為使者。

translations.literal: Chang was not by nature a man of backbone; hearing Southerners say that the elder brother was already a general while the younger brother was an envoy.
translations.idiomatic: Chang was not a man of iron will by nature; when he heard Southerners say that his elder brother was already a general while he himself was the envoy.

sentences.zh: 乃大恐怖，淚汗交橫。

translations.literal: He was greatly terrified; tears and sweat streamed together.
translations.idiomatic: He was seized with terror, tears and sweat streaming down together.

sentences.zh: 鸞以腐米臭魚莝豆供之。

translations.literal: Luan supplied him with rotten rice, stinking fish, and bean fodder.
translations.idiomatic: Luan fed them rotten rice, stinking fish, and bean fodder.

sentences.zh: 而謁者張思寧辭氣謇諤，曾不屈撓，遂以壯烈死於館中。

translations.literal: Attendant Zhang Sining, however, was stern and upright in speech and countenance and never bent or yielded, and so died heroically in the lodge.
translations.idiomatic: Attendant Zhang Sining, however, spoke with stern and upright bearing and never yielded, and so died a heroic death in the envoy's lodge.

sentences.zh: 昶還，高祖責之曰：「銜命之禮，有死無辱，雖流放海隅，猶宜抱節致殞。

translations.literal: When Chang returned, Emperor Xiaowen reproached him, saying: "The ritual of bearing the mandate holds that one may die but not be disgraced; though exiled to the sea's edge, one should still hold integrity unto death.
translations.idiomatic: When Chang returned, Emperor Xiaowen rebuked him: "The duty of bearing the imperial mandate is death before disgrace; even exiled to the sea's edge one should hold to integrity unto death.

sentences.zh: 卿不能長纓羇首，已是可恨。

translations.literal: You could not bind yourself with the long cord like a captive—already hateful.
translations.idiomatic: That you could not bind yourself with the long cord like a captive is hateful enough.

sentences.zh: 何乃俛眉飲啄，自同犬馬。

translations.literal: Why then bow your brows and eat pecked food, making yourself the same as dogs and horses?
translations.idiomatic: Why then bow your head and eat whatever is thrown before you, living like a dog or a horse?

sentences.zh: 有生必死，修短幾何。

translations.literal: Life once born must die; long or short—how much is there?
translations.idiomatic: Life once given must end; long or short, what difference does it make?

sentences.zh: 卿若殺身成名，貽之竹素，何如甘彼芻菽，以辱君父乎？

translations.literal: If you had killed your body to establish your name and left it to bamboo and silk, how would that compare to willingly accepting that fodder and disgracing lord and father?
translations.idiomatic: If you had died to win a name and left your story to be written on bamboo and silk, how would that compare with willingly accepting their fodder and disgracing your sovereign and your father?

sentences.zh: 縱不遠慚蘇武，寧不近愧思寧！

translations.literal: Even if you are not ashamed before Su Wu from afar, are you not ashamed before Sining from near at hand!
translations.idiomatic: Even if you feel no shame before Su Wu in the distant past, can you feel no shame before Sining at your side!

sentences.zh: 」昶對曰：「臣器乏陸、隨，忝使閩越。

translations.literal: "] Chang replied: "Your servant's capacity falls short of Lu and Sui; I humbly served as envoy to Minyue.
translations.idiomatic: Chang replied: "My capacity falls far short of men like Lu Ji and Su Wu; I was unworthy to serve as envoy to the southern lands.

sentences.zh: 屬蕭鸞昏狂，誅戮無道。

translations.literal: It happened that Xiao Luan was deluded and mad, slaughtering without principle.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Luan was deluded and violent and slaughtered without restraint.

sentences.zh: 恐不得仰奉明時，歸養老母，苟存尺蠖，屈以求伸。

translations.literal: I feared I would not be able respectfully to serve the enlightened age and return to support my old mother; I kept the inchworm alive, bending in order to stretch.
translations.idiomatic: I feared I would not be able to serve the enlightened age and return to care for my aged mother; like the inchworm I preserved my life, bending now so that I might straighten later.

sentences.zh: 負辱朝命，罪宜萬死，乞歸司寇，伏聽斧鉞。

translations.literal: Bearing disgrace to the court's mandate, my crime deserves ten thousand deaths; I beg to be returned to the Minister of Justice and await the axe and halberd.
translations.idiomatic: I have disgraced the imperial mandate and deserve death ten thousand times over; I beg to be handed over to the Minister of Justice and await execution.

sentences.zh: 」遂見罷黜。

translations.literal: "] He was then dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: He was then dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 久之，復除彭城王友，轉祕書丞。

translations.literal: After a long time, he was again appointed Friend of the Prince of Pengcheng and transferred to Secretariat Assistant.
translations.idiomatic: After a long interval he was again appointed Friend of the Prince of Pengcheng, then transferred to Secretariat Assistant.

sentences.zh: 景明初，除中書侍郎，遷給事黃門侍郎、本州大中正。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jingming, he was appointed Attendant Gentleman of the Central Secretariat and promoted to Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate for Presenting Affairs and Chief Arbiter of his home province.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Jingming era he was appointed Attendant Gentleman of the Central Secretariat, then promoted to Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate for Presenting Affairs and Chief Arbiter of his home province.

sentences.zh: 昶請外祿，世宗不許。

translations.literal: Chang requested an external stipend; Emperor Shizong did not consent.
translations.idiomatic: Chang requested an appointment with external emoluments, but Emperor Shizong refused.

sentences.zh: 遷散騎常侍，兼尚書。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Regular Attendant at Large and made concurrent Minister.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Regular Attendant at Large and made concurrent Minister.

sentences.zh: 時洛陽縣獲白鼠。

translations.literal: At that time Luoyang County captured a white rat.
translations.idiomatic: At that time a white rat was caught in Luoyang County.

sentences.zh: 昶奏曰：

translations.literal: Chang memorialized, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Chang submitted a memorial, saying:

sentences.zh: 謹案瑞典，外鎮刺史、二千石、令長不祗上命，刻暴百姓，人民怨嗟，則白鼠至。

translations.literal: I respectfully investigate the Ruidian: when territorial governors, Two-Thousand-Bushel officials, and magistrates fail to revere the sovereign's commands, are harsh and cruel toward the common people, and the populace groans in resentment, then white rats appear.
translations.idiomatic: I have carefully consulted the Ruidian, which records that when provincial governors, officials of two-thousand-bushel rank, and local magistrates fail to honor the throne's commands and treat the people with harsh cruelty until the populace groan in resentment, white rats appear.

sentences.zh: 臣聞禎不虛見，德合必符；

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that auspicious omens do not appear without cause, and when virtue matches, they must correspond;
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that auspicious signs never appear without cause, and that when virtue is in harmony, the signs must correspond;

sentences.zh: 妖不妄出，咎彰則至。

translations.literal: portents do not emerge wantonly—when guilt becomes manifest, they arrive.
translations.idiomatic: nor do portents arise at random: when guilt is plain, they come.

sentences.zh: 是以古之人君，或怠瑞以失德，或祗變而立功，斯乃萬古之殷鑒，千齡之炯誡。

translations.literal: Therefore sovereigns of old either neglected auspicious signs and lost virtue, or reverently responded to change and established merit—this is a stern mirror through ten thousand ages, a bright warning across a thousand generations.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the sovereigns of antiquity either neglected auspicious omens and lost their virtue, or reverently heeded change and achieved merit—a stern mirror for all ages, a bright warning across a thousand years.

sentences.zh: 比者，災氣作沴，恒陽虧度，陛下流如傷之慈，降納隍之旨，哀百姓之無辜，引在予之深責。

translations.literal: Recently calamitous qi has wrought harm, constant yang has fallen short of its measure. Your Majesty has issued compassion flowing like wound-tending, and decrees drawing the fallen from the ditches, grieving the innocence of the common people and taking upon yourself the deep blame that lies with the ruler.
translations.idiomatic: Recently calamity has spread and the sun's courses have fallen out of measure, yet Your Majesty has shown compassion tender as care for a wound, issued edicts in the spirit of drawing the fallen from the ditches, grieved for the innocent among the people, and taken upon yourself the sovereign's deep burden of blame.

sentences.zh: 舉賢黜佞之詔，道映於堯先；

translations.literal: Your edict to promote the worthy and remove the sycophantic reflects the Way even before Yao;
translations.idiomatic: Your decree to raise the worthy and dismiss the sycophantic shines with a virtue that outshines even Yao;

sentences.zh: 進思納諫之言，事光於舜右。

translations.literal: your words of advancing through reflection and accepting remonstrance put the matter in brilliance even to Shun's right.
translations.idiomatic: your counsel to advance through reflection and accept remonstrance places your conduct in a light that eclipses even Shun.

sentences.zh: 伏讀明旨，俯觀徵譴，敢布庸瞽，以陳萬一。

translations.literal: I prostrate myself to read your clear intent and bow to observe the signs of warning; I dare offer my mediocre blindness to set forth one part in ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Prostrate, I have read your enlightened decree and pondered the signs of warning; I dare lay before you my humble ignorance in the hope of offering even one word in ten thousand that may help.

sentences.zh: 竊惟一夫之耕，食裁充口；

translations.literal: I venture to consider that one man's plowing yields food barely enough to fill the mouth;
translations.idiomatic: Consider: one man's plowing yields barely enough to fill his mouth;

sentences.zh: 一婦之織，衣止蔽形。

translations.literal: one woman's weaving yields clothes barely enough to cover the body.
translations.idiomatic: one woman's weaving yields cloth barely enough to cover her body.

sentences.zh: 年租歲調，則惟常理，此外徵求，於何取足？

translations.literal: The annual rent and yearly levies are the only normal obligations—beyond these, whence is enough to supply further exactions?
translations.idiomatic: The annual rent and yearly levies are the normal burden alone; beyond them, where is the surplus to meet still more exactions?

sentences.zh: 然自比年以來，兵革屢動。

translations.literal: Yet since recent years military affairs have stirred repeatedly.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in recent years war has stirred again and again.

sentences.zh: 荊揚二州，屯戍不息；

translations.literal: In Jing and Yang provinces, garrison duty has not ceased;
translations.idiomatic: In Jing and Yang the garrisons have never rested;

sentences.zh: 鍾離、義陽，師旅相繼。

translations.literal: at Zhongli and Yiyang, armies have followed one after another.
translations.idiomatic: at Zhongli and Yiyang armies have marched in unbroken succession.

sentences.zh: 兼荊蠻凶狡，王師薄伐，暴露原野，經秋淹夏。

translations.literal: Moreover the barbarians of Jing are fierce and cunning; the imperial army made a shallow campaign against them, exposed on the open fields through autumn into summer.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile the Man of Jing are fierce and treacherous; the imperial armies have campaigned against them, bivouacking in the open fields from spring through autumn.

sentences.zh: 汝潁之地，率戶從戎；

translations.literal: In the lands of Ru and Ying, households by whole villages have gone to war;
translations.idiomatic: In Ru and Ying nearly every household has been called to arms;

sentences.zh: 河冀之境，連丁轉運。

translations.literal: in the frontier of He and Ji, men in unbroken train have hauled supplies.
translations.idiomatic: in He and Ji men have been conscripted in unbroken chains to haul supplies.

sentences.zh: 又戰不必勝，加之退負，死喪離曠，十室而九。

translations.literal: Moreover battles were not necessarily won, and on top of that came retreat and defeat; deaths, losses, separation, and desolation—nine houses out of ten.
translations.idiomatic: Battles were not always won; rout and defeat followed, and death, loss, and separation left nine houses in ten empty.

sentences.zh: 細役煩徭，日月滋甚；

translations.literal: petty corvée labor and burdensome service have grown day by day and month by month;
translations.idiomatic: Petty duties and onerous corvée have grown heavier with each passing day;

sentences.zh: 苛兵酷吏，因逞威福。

translations.literal: harsh soldiers and cruel clerks have thereupon displayed their power and favor.
translations.idiomatic: harsh soldiers and cruel officials have seized the moment to abuse their power.

sentences.zh: 至使通原遙畛，田蕪罕耘；

translations.literal: to the point that across the plains and distant fields, weed-choked farmland is rarely tilled;
translations.idiomatic: So that across distant plains and far-off fields tillage has been abandoned and fields run to weeds;

sentences.zh: 連村接閈，蠶飢莫食。

translations.literal: village linked to village and lane joined to lane, silkworms starve with none to feed them.
translations.idiomatic: village after village and lane after lane, silkworms starve for lack of care.

sentences.zh: 而監司因公以貪求，豪強恃私而逼掠。

translations.literal: Yet overseers, using public office, have grasped for greed; the powerful, relying on private interest, have pressed and plundered.
translations.idiomatic: Overseers exploit their office to extort; the powerful rely on private ties to coerce and plunder.

sentences.zh: 遂令鬻裋褐以益千金之資，制口腹而充一朝之急。

translations.literal: Thus people have been made to sell coarse hemp garments to augment funds of a thousand gold, and constrain belly and mouth to meet a single day's emergency.
translations.idiomatic: Families sell their coarse garments to raise sums worth a thousand in gold, and go hungry to meet a single day's emergency.

sentences.zh: 此皆由牧守令長多失其人，郡闕黃霸之君，縣無魯恭之宰，不思所以安民，正思所以潤屋。

translations.literal: All this is because prefects, governors, and magistrates are mostly wrong men for their posts—commanderies lack rulers like Huang Ba, counties lack administrators like Lu Gong; they do not think how to settle the people, but only how to enrich their houses.
translations.idiomatic: All this stems from the wrong men holding office as governors, prefects, and magistrates: the commanderies have no Huang Ba, the counties no Lu Gong. They give no thought to settling the people, only to fattening their own households.

sentences.zh: 故士女呼嗟，相望於道路；

translations.literal: Therefore men and women sigh in lament, visible to one another on the roads;
translations.idiomatic: Men and women lament within sight of one another on every road;

sentences.zh: 守宰暴貪，風聞於魏闕。

translations.literal: the cruelty and greed of governors and magistrates have reached the imperial gate by rumor.
translations.idiomatic: and reports of the cruelty and greed of local officials have reached the imperial gate.

sentences.zh: 往歲法官案驗，多挂刑網，謂必顯戮，以明勸誡。

translations.literal: In past years when legal officers investigated cases, many fell into the penal net; it was said they would surely suffer conspicuous execution to clarify exhortation and warning.
translations.idiomatic: In past years when the legal offices investigated cases, many officials were caught in the penal net and were expected to face public execution as a clear warning to others.

sentences.zh: 然後遣使覆訊，公違憲典。

translations.literal: Yet afterward envoys were sent to re-examine, publicly violating the statutes.
translations.idiomatic: Yet afterward imperial envoys were sent to re-examine the cases, openly violating the law.

sentences.zh: 或承風挾請，輕樹私恩；

translations.literal: Some rode the prevailing wind to press petitions and lightly planted private favor;
translations.idiomatic: Some seized the moment to press petitions and lightly offered private favors;

sentences.zh: 或容情受賄，輒施己惠。

translations.literal: some indulged feelings and accepted bribes, then bestowing their own grace.
translations.idiomatic: others turned a blind eye for bribes and granted favors of their own.

sentences.zh: 御史所劾，皆言誣枉；

translations.literal: What the censor impeached, all was called false and unjust;
translations.idiomatic: Impeachments from the censorate were dismissed as false and unjust;

sentences.zh: 申雪罪人，更云清白。

translations.literal: guilty men vindicated were further said to be pure and clean.
translations.idiomatic: and when guilty men were cleared, they were proclaimed innocent instead.

sentences.zh: 長侮上之源，滋陵下之路。

translations.literal: This lengthens the source by which superiors are insulted and nourishes the path by which inferiors are bullied.
translations.idiomatic: This only lengthens the road by which authority is mocked above and emboldens bullying below.

sentences.zh: 忠清之人，見之而自怠；

translations.literal: Loyal and clean men, seeing this, slacken of themselves;
translations.idiomatic: The loyal and upright, seeing this, lose heart;

sentences.zh: 犯暴之夫，聞之以益快。

translations.literal: men who violate and rage, hearing of it, grow all the more pleased.
translations.idiomatic: while violent offenders, hearing of it, grow all the bolder.

sentences.zh: 白鼠之至，信而有徵矣。

translations.literal: The arrival of the white rat—truly there is evidence for it.
translations.idiomatic: The coming of the white rat is, it seems, no empty sign.

sentences.zh: 伏願陛下垂叡哲之鑒，察妖災之起。

translations.literal: I prostrate myself and hope Your Majesty will let fall the mirror of sagacious insight and discern the rise of portents and calamity.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to apply the mirror of your sagacious insight and discern why this portent has arisen.

sentences.zh: 延對公卿，廣詢庶政；

translations.literal: Extend audience to the high ministers and broadly inquire into the myriad affairs of government;
translations.idiomatic: Summon the high ministers for counsel and inquire broadly into public affairs;

sentences.zh: 引見樞納，博求民隱。

translations.literal: summon and receive those close at the pivot of counsel, and broadly seek the people's hidden grievances.
translations.idiomatic: receive those who hold the keys of counsel and seek widely the grievances the people hide.

sentences.zh: 存問孤寡，去其苛碎；

translations.literal: visit and comfort the orphaned and widowed, and remove petty and oppressive regulations;
translations.idiomatic: Comfort the orphaned and the widowed, and remove petty and oppressive regulations;

sentences.zh: 輕徭省賦，與民休息。

translations.literal: lighten corvée and reduce taxes, and give the people rest.
translations.idiomatic: lighten corvée and reduce taxes, and give the people respite.

sentences.zh: 貞良忠讜，置之於朝；

translations.literal: Place the upright, the good, the loyal, and the forthright in the court;
translations.idiomatic: Set the upright, the good, the loyal, and the forthright in office at court;

sentences.zh: 姦回貪佞，棄之於市。

translations.literal: cast the wicked, the crooked, the greedy, and the sycophantic out in the marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: and cast the wicked, the crooked, the greedy, and the sycophantic out to public shame.

sentences.zh: 則九官勿戒而恒敬，百縣不嚴而自肅，士女欣欣，人有望矣。

translations.literal: Then the Nine Officers need no admonition yet remain always reverent; the hundred counties need no severity yet discipline themselves; men and women rejoice, and the people have hope.
translations.idiomatic: Then the Nine Officers will need no admonition yet remain always reverent; the hundred counties will need no severity yet govern themselves; men and women will rejoice, and the people will have hope again.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「朕纂承鴻緒，伏膺寶曆，思靖八方，惠康四海。

translations.literal: An edict said: "I have succeeded to the great inheritance, bowed to receive the precious calendar, and think to pacify the eight directions and bring kindness and comfort to the four seas.
translations.idiomatic: An edict said: "I have succeeded to the great throne, received the sacred calendar, and seek to pacify all lands and bring kindness and comfort to the four seas.

sentences.zh: 當必世之期，麟鳳不降；

translations.literal: At a time that should be the age of perfect peace, qilin and phoenix do not descend;
translations.idiomatic: At a time that should be an age of perfect peace, no qilin or phoenix has appeared;

sentences.zh: 屬勝殘之會，白鼠告咎。

translations.literal: in a season suited to overcoming cruelty and slaughter, white rats proclaim guilt.
translations.idiomatic: yet in this season when cruelty should be overcome, the white rat announces guilt.

sentences.zh: 萬邦有罪，實唯朕躬。

translations.literal: The myriad states have guilt—truly it lies with me alone.
translations.idiomatic: If the myriad realms bear guilt, the fault is mine alone.

sentences.zh: 尚書敷納機猷，獻替是寄，讜言有聞，朕實嘉美。

translations.literal: The Minister has spread and received pivotal counsel; replacing and offering advice is his charge; forthright words have reached my ears—I truly commend this excellence."
translations.idiomatic: The Minister has offered pivotal counsel and been entrusted with the duty of remonstrance; I have heard your forthright words and greatly commend them."

sentences.zh: 」轉侍中，又兼吏部尚書，尋即正，仍侍中。

translations.literal: "] He was transferred to Palace Attendant, and again made concurrent Minister of the Ministry of Personnel; shortly afterward he received the regular appointment, while still serving as Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Palace Attendant and again made concurrent Minister of Personnel; shortly afterward he received the regular appointment while continuing as Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 昶守職而已，無所激揚也。

translations.literal: Chang merely guarded his office and did nothing to rouse or promote.
translations.idiomatic: Chang merely performed his duties and did nothing to stir reform.

sentences.zh: 與侍中元暉等更相朋附，為世宗所寵，時論鄙之。

translations.literal: With Palace Attendant Yuan Hui and others he alternately banded together in faction; favored by Emperor Shizong, he was despised in public opinion.
translations.idiomatic: He and Palace Attendant Yuan Hui and others formed a mutual faction; favored by Emperor Shizong, he was held in contempt by public opinion.

sentences.zh: 出除鎮東將軍、徐州刺史。

translations.literal: He was sent out and appointed General Who Pacifies the East and Governor of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out and appointed General Who Pacifies the East and Governor of Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 永平四年夏，昶表曰：「蕭衍琅邪郡民王萬壽等款誠內結，潛來詣臣，云朐山戍今將交換，有可圖之機。

translations.literal: In the summer of the fourth year of Yongping, Chang submitted a memorial, saying: "Xiao Yan's subjects Wang Wanshou and others of Langye Commandery have pledged sincerity and joined within; they came secretly to me and said the Qiu Mountain garrison is now about to be exchanged, and there is an opportunity that may be seized.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the fourth year of Yongping, Chang submitted a memorial: "Wang Wanshou and others, subjects of Langye under Xiao Yan, have pledged their loyalty from within. They came secretly to me and reported that the Qiu Mountain garrison is soon to be exchanged—a moment we may seize.

sentences.zh: 臣即許以旌賞，遣其還入。

translations.literal: Your servant at once promised them banners and rewards and sent them back inside.
translations.idiomatic: I promised them honors and rewards and sent them back.

sentences.zh: 至三月二十四夜，萬壽等奬率同盟，攻掩朐城，斬衍輔國將軍，琅邪、東莞二郡太守，帶朐山戍主劉晣并將士四十餘人，傳首至州。

translations.literal: By the night of the twenty-fourth day of the third month, Wanshou and others led their allies in assault and captured Qiu City, beheaded Xiao Yan's General Who Supports the State, Grand Administrator of the two commanderies of Langye and Dongguan, and Concurrent Commander of the Qiu Mountain Garrison, Liu Xi, along with more than forty officers and troops, and sent the heads to the province.
translations.idiomatic: On the night of the twenty-fourth day of the third month, Wanshou and his allies stormed Qiu City and beheaded Liu Xi, Xiao Yan's General Who Supports the State and Grand Administrator of Langye and Dongguan, who also commanded the Qiu Mountain garrison, along with more than forty officers and men; their heads were sent to my provincial headquarters.

sentences.zh: 臣即遣兼郯城戍副張天惠率驍勇二百，徑往赴之。

translations.literal: Your servant at once sent the deputy commander of the Tancheng garrison, Zhang Tianhui, leading two hundred picked brave men, directly to rush to the scene.
translations.idiomatic: I immediately sent Zhang Tianhui, deputy commander of the Tancheng garrison, with two hundred picked warriors to hurry to their aid.

sentences.zh: 琅邪諸戍絡繹繼援，而衍郁洲已遣二軍以拒天惠。

translations.literal: The garrisons of Langye came in unbroken train to reinforce, while Xiao Yan from Yuzhou had already dispatched two armies to oppose Tianhui.
translations.idiomatic: The Langye garrisons sent reinforcements in unbroken succession, but Xiao Yan had already sent two armies from Yuzhou to block Tianhui.

sentences.zh: 天惠與萬壽等內外齊擊，俘斬數百，便即據城。

translations.literal: Tianhui with Wanshou and others struck together from within and without, captured and beheaded several hundred, and then at once held the city."
translations.idiomatic: Tianhui and Wanshou attacked together from within and without, capturing and slaying several hundred men, and held the city."

sentences.zh: 」詔昶曰：「彭宋地接邊疆，勢連淮海，威禦之術，功在不易。

translations.literal: "] An edict to Chang said: "The Peng-Song region borders the frontier; its position connects with the Huai and the sea. The art of intimidating and defending is an achievement not easily won.
translations.idiomatic: An edict to Chang said: "The Peng-Song region lies on the frontier, its position tied to the Huai River and the sea. To intimidate and defend it is no easy achievement.

sentences.zh: 朐山險塞，寇之要防，水陸交湊，揚、郁路衝，畜聚凶徒，虔劉邊鄙，青、光、齊、兗每罹其患。

translations.literal: Qiu Mountain is a perilous pass and the enemy's key defense; water and land converge, the routes of Yang and Yu clash—harboring gathered villains, devoutly plundering the border marches; Qing, Guang, Qi, and Yan suffer its harm each in turn.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu Mountain is a perilous stronghold and the enemy's vital defense, where land and water routes meet at the crossroads of Yang and Yu. It has gathered bandits and ravaged the frontiers, and Qing, Guang, Qi, and Yan suffer from it again and again.

sentences.zh: 卿妙算既敷，克城殄眾，展疆闢土，何善如之。

translations.literal: Your subtle plans have already been laid out; you took the city and wiped out the masses, expanded the frontier and opened land—what goodness equals this?
translations.idiomatic: You laid your plans wisely, took the city, destroyed the enemy, and expanded our territory—what could be better?

sentences.zh: 庸勳之懋，朕用嘉止。

translations.literal: For your meritorious labor's excellence I am moved to praise and halt here.
translations.idiomatic: For such distinguished merit I commend you with highest praise.

sentences.zh: 故遣左右直長閻遵業具宣往懷。

translations.literal: Therefore I send Chief of the Left and Right Attendants Yan Zunye fully to declare my former regard.
translations.idiomatic: I have therefore sent Chief Attendant Yan Zunye to convey my sentiments in full.

sentences.zh: 此戍郁洲之本，存亡所繫。

translations.literal: This garrison is the root of Yuzhou; on it survival and destruction depend.
translations.idiomatic: This garrison is the foundation of Yuzhou; its survival hangs upon it.

sentences.zh: 今既失守，有不存之心；

translations.literal: Now that it has been lost, the enemy has a mind of not preserving us;
translations.idiomatic: Now that it has been taken, they will not be content to stop there;

sentences.zh: 彼見扼喉，將圖救援之計。

translations.literal: seeing their throat gripped, they will scheme plans of rescue.
translations.idiomatic: finding their throat seized, they will seek some means of rescue.

sentences.zh: 今水雨盛行，宜須防守。

translations.literal: Now water and rain prevail widely—it is fitting to defend.
translations.idiomatic: With the rains at their height, you must hold the position.

sentences.zh: 卿可深思擬捍之規，攘敵之略，使還具聞。」

translations.literal: You may deeply consider plans for resisting and strategies for driving off the enemy, and send back full report."
translations.idiomatic: Consider deeply how to hold and how to repel the enemy, and report back in full."

sentences.zh: 昶又表：「蕭衍將張稷、馬仙琕、陰虔和等各領精兵，分屯諸堰；

translations.literal: Chang submitted another memorial: "Xiao Yan's generals Zhang Ji, Ma Xianbi, and Yin Qianhe each command picked troops and garrison the various dams separately;
translations.idiomatic: Chang submitted another memorial: "Xiao Yan's generals Zhang Ji, Ma Xianbi, and Yin Qianhe each lead picked troops posted at the various dams;

sentences.zh: 昌義之、張惠紹、王神念、王茂光承彼傳信，續發建鄴。

translations.literal: Chang Yizhi, Zhang Huishao, Wang Shenshen, and Wang Maoguang, receiving their relayed messages, continue dispatching troops from Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: Chang Yizhi, Zhang Huishao, Wang Shenshen, and Wang Maoguang, acting on their dispatches, are sending reinforcements from Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 自存之計，并歸於此。

translations.literal: Their plans for self-preservation all converge on this.
translations.idiomatic: Their entire plan for survival depends on this.

sentences.zh: 量力準寇，事恐不輕。

translations.literal: Measuring strength against the enemy, the affair is feared not light.
translations.idiomatic: Judging by the forces on both sides, this will be no small affair.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 此兵九千，賊眾四萬，名將健士，遠近畢集，邀憑雨熱，[6]決死來戰，藉眾乘凶，希固巢穴。

translations.literal: Here are nine thousand troops, the enemy host forty thousand—famous generals and stout warriors gathered from near and far; relying on rain and heat, they will fight to the death, borrowing numbers and riding misfortune, hoping to secure their nest.
translations.idiomatic: We have nine thousand men; the enemy may number forty thousand, with famous generals and stout warriors gathered from near and far. They will rely on the rain and heat to fight to the death, use their numbers to exploit our danger, and hope to hold their stronghold.

sentences.zh: 所以傾國而舉，非為朐山，將恐王師固六里，據湖衝，南截淮浦，勢崩難測，海利鹽物，交闕常貢。

translations.literal: For this reason they mobilize the whole state—not for Qiu Mountain alone, but fearing the imperial army will hold Liuli, seize the lake crossing, slice the Huai's banks to the south—the momentum of collapse is hard to measure; sea profits and salt goods, and the constant tribute from Jiao, would be cut off.
translations.idiomatic: They are mobilizing the entire state—not merely for Qiu Mountain, but because they fear our armies may hold Liuli, command the lake crossings, and cut the Huai's southern bank. The consequences are hard to foretell: profits from the sea and salt, and the tribute route of Jiao, would all be severed.

sentences.zh: 所慮在大，有必爭之心。

translations.literal: What is feared is great; there is a mind that must contend.
translations.idiomatic: Their concern is great; they mean to fight for this at all costs.

sentences.zh: 若皇家經略，方有所討，必須簡將增兵，加益糧仗，與之亢擬。

translations.literal: If the imperial house's strategy is indeed set on punitive campaign, it must select generals and increase troops, add provisions and weapons, and match them in rivalry.
translations.idiomatic: If the throne intends a full campaign, we must select commanders, add troops and supplies, and meet them on equal terms.

sentences.zh: 相持至秋，天麾一動，開拓為易。

translations.literal: Holding each other until autumn, when Heaven's banner moves once, expansion will be easy.
translations.idiomatic: Hold through autumn, and when the imperial banner moves, expansion will come easily.

sentences.zh: 圖南之計，事本在今，請增兵六千、米十萬石；

translations.literal: The plan to expand southward fundamentally belongs to this moment; I request six thousand additional troops and one hundred thousand shi of grain;
translations.idiomatic: The plan to push south must begin now. I request six thousand additional troops and one hundred thousand shi of grain;

sentences.zh: 如其不也，伏聽朝議。

translations.literal: if not granted, I prostrate myself to await court deliberation."
translations.idiomatic: if that cannot be granted, I await the court's deliberation."

sentences.zh: 」昶又表：「賊徒大集，眾旅強盛，置柵朐山，屯守門井，并圍固城，晝夜連戰。

translations.literal: "] Chang submitted another memorial: "The rebel bandits have massed in great numbers; their hosts are strong. They have set palisades at Qiu Mountain, garrisoned the gates and wells, and also besieged Gucheng, fighting through day and night.
translations.idiomatic: Chang submitted another memorial: "The enemy has massed in strength, set palisades at Qiu Mountain, garrisoned Menjing, and invested Gucheng, fighting day and night without cease.

sentences.zh: 恐狡勢既強，後難除揃。

translations.literal: I fear that once their cunning force has grown strong, afterward it will be hard to eliminate and level.
translations.idiomatic: I fear that once their strength grows, they will be difficult to destroy later.

sentences.zh: 輒欲令征虜將軍趙遐率勒見兵，與之決勝。

translations.literal: I would have General Who Pacifies the Barbarians Zhao Xia lead the available troops and decide victory with them.
translations.idiomatic: I propose that General Who Pacifies the Barbarians Zhao Xia lead our present forces and fight them to a decision.

sentences.zh: 遐慮眾少不敵，若一舉失利，則眾心挫怯，求待大眾俱至，奮銳擊之。

translations.literal: Xia feared his numbers were few and he could not match them; if one effort failed, the army's hearts would be crushed and timid. He sought to wait until the great host all arrived and then strike them with sharp valor.
translations.idiomatic: Xia feared our numbers were too few; one defeat would break the army's spirit, so he wished to wait until the main force arrived and then strike with full vigor.

sentences.zh: 竊謂此謀，非為孟浪。

translations.literal: I venture to say this plan is not rash.
translations.idiomatic: I believe this plan is not rash.

sentences.zh: 且臣本奉朝規，令相拒守，以待涼月。

translations.literal: Moreover I originally received the court's rule, ordered to hold each other off in guard, awaiting the cool month.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover I was originally ordered by the court to hold and wait until the cooler months.

sentences.zh: 今歲已云秋，高風漸舉，經算大圖，時事既至。

translations.literal: Now the year is already autumn; the high winds gradually rise; the great design reckoned beforehand—the season has arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Autumn has already come, the high winds are rising, and the grand strategy we planned for is now at hand.

sentences.zh: 且鮑口以東，陸運無閡，朐、固之間，本無停潦，宜時掩擊邊陲。

translations.literal: Moreover east of Baokou, transport by land is unobstructed; between Qiu and Gu there are originally no standing floods—it is fitting to seize the moment for a sudden strike on the border.
translations.idiomatic: East of Baokou overland transport is clear; between Qiu and Gu there is no standing water. This is the time to strike the border positions.

sentences.zh: 而賊自夏以來，貫甲不歇，從六里以北，城柵相連，役使兵人，便已疲殆。

translations.literal: Yet since summer the enemy have worn armor without cease; from north of Liuli, walled palisades join one to another—the labor pressed upon the soldiers has already exhausted them.
translations.idiomatic: Yet since summer the enemy have worn armor without rest; north of Liuli their walls and palisades run unbroken, and their soldiers are already worn out from constant labor.

sentences.zh: 若大眾臨之，必可禽捷。

translations.literal: If the great host presses upon them, capture will surely come swiftly.
translations.idiomatic: If our main force presses them now, a quick victory is certain.

sentences.zh: 一城退潰，眾壘土崩，乘勝圖之，易於振朽。

translations.literal: When one city retreats and collapses, the many forts fall like earthen walls; pursuing victory to plan further is easier than shaking decayed wood.
translations.idiomatic: If one city falls, the rest will collapse like earthen walls; pressed while they are in rout, the rest will break like rotten wood.

sentences.zh: 脫兵不速至，長彼熾心，軍士憂惶，自生異議。

translations.literal: If troops do not arrive swiftly, the enemy's fierce heart will lengthen; the soldiers will worry in dread and of themselves give rise to dissent.
translations.idiomatic: If reinforcements do not come quickly, the enemy's resolve will only harden, our soldiers will grow anxious, and dissent will arise in our ranks.

sentences.zh: 請速簡配，以及事機。

translations.literal: I beg for swift selection and allotment, to meet the moment's opportunity."
translations.idiomatic: I beg that troops be selected and dispatched at once, before the moment is lost."

sentences.zh: 」詔曰：「克獲朐山，計本於昶，乘勝之規，終宜有寄。

translations.literal: "] An edict said: "The plan to capture Qiu Mountain originally rested with Chang; the scheme to press the victory should ultimately be entrusted to someone.
translations.idiomatic: An edict said: "The plan to take Qiu Mountain began with Chang; the strategy to press our advantage should ultimately rest with him.

sentences.zh: 是以起兵之始，即委處分，前機經略，一以任之。

translations.literal: Therefore from the beginning of raising troops, I at once entrusted him with disposition; the forward planning of strategy—all was entrusted to him.
translations.idiomatic: From the moment the campaign began I entrusted the disposition of forces to him and gave him full authority over the forward strategy.

sentences.zh: 今既請兵，理宜速遂。

translations.literal: Now that he has requested troops, it is fitting in principle to fulfill this swiftly.
translations.idiomatic: Now that he has requested troops, they should be sent at once.

sentences.zh: 可遣冀、定、瀛、相四州中品羽林、虎賁四千人赴之。」

translations.literal: Four thousand mid-grade Yulin and Huben guard soldiers from the four provinces of Ji, Ding, Ying, and Xiang may be dispatched to go there."
translations.idiomatic: Dispatch four thousand mid-grade Yulin and Huben guards from Ji, Ding, Ying, and Xiang to join him."

sentences.zh: 又詔昶曰：「朐山之克，實由於卿，開疆拓土，實為長策。

translations.literal: Again an edict to Chang said: "The capture of Qiu Mountain was truly due to you; opening the frontier and expanding territory is truly the long-term strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Another edict to Chang said: "The capture of Qiu Mountain was truly your doing; opening and expanding the frontier is the sound long-term strategy.

sentences.zh: 然經討未服，非卿而誰？

translations.literal: Yet the pacification campaigns are not yet complete—if not you, then who?
translations.idiomatic: Yet the rebels are not yet fully subdued—who but you can finish the work?

sentences.zh: 而蟻徒送死，規侵王略，天亡小賊，數在無遠。

translations.literal: Those ant-like rabble rush to their deaths, plotting to invade our royal domain; Heaven will destroy the petty bandits, and their doom is not far off.
translations.idiomatic: Those ant-like rebels rush headlong to their deaths, scheming to encroach on our imperial territory; Heaven will destroy these petty bandits, and their end is near.

sentences.zh: 故前者命卿親臨指授，尋以卿疾未瘳，且待消息。

translations.literal: Therefore earlier I ordered you to come in person to direct and instruct; soon after, because your illness had not yet healed, I waited for word.
translations.idiomatic: That is why I earlier ordered you to take command in person; when your illness had not yet healed, I held off and waited for news.

sentences.zh: 今既痊復，宜遵前旨，秉戈揮銳，殄寇為懷。

translations.literal: Now that you have recovered, you should follow the earlier intent, take up weapons and wield sharp blades, with exterminating the enemy as your purpose.
translations.idiomatic: Now that you have recovered, you should carry out my earlier orders: take up arms, lead your troops, and make the destruction of the enemy your sole aim.

sentences.zh: 已發虎旅五萬，應機電赴，指辰而至，遂卿本請。

translations.literal: I have already dispatched fifty thousand tiger troops to rush like lightning as the moment demands, to arrive within the appointed time, fulfilling your original request.
translations.idiomatic: I have already sent fifty thousand elite troops to move swiftly as circumstances require and arrive on schedule, granting the reinforcements you originally requested.

sentences.zh: 截彼東南，亮委高算。

translations.literal: Cut off their southeast—I clearly entrust the grand strategy to you.
translations.idiomatic: Sever their hold on the southeast; the overall strategy I now place entirely in your hands.

sentences.zh: 」又詔昶曰：「取朐置戍，並是卿計，始終成敗，悉歸於卿。

translations.literal: "] Again an edict to Chang said: "Taking Qiu and establishing a garrison were both your plan; from beginning to end, success or failure rests entirely with you.
translations.idiomatic: " Another edict to Chang said: "Capturing Qiu and posting a garrison were your plans; from first to last, success or failure rests entirely with you.

sentences.zh: 卿以兵少請益，今已遂卿本意。

translations.literal: You requested reinforcements because your troops were too few; now your original wish has been fulfilled.
translations.idiomatic: You asked for more troops because your force was too small; that request has now been granted.

sentences.zh: 如聞東唐陸道甚狹，一軌之外，皆是大水。

translations.literal: I have heard that the land route through eastern Tang is very narrow, and beyond the width of a single cart track lies nothing but great waters.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that the land route through eastern Tang is extremely narrow—beyond a single cart track, there is only open water.

sentences.zh: 彼必據之，以斷軍路。

translations.literal: The enemy will surely hold it to cut off our army's route.
translations.idiomatic: They will surely hold that ground to sever our line of march.

sentences.zh: 若已如此，更設何策？

translations.literal: If it is already so, what further plan should be devised?
translations.idiomatic: If matters stand as you describe, what alternative strategy do you propose?

sentences.zh: 其軍奇兵變，遽以表聞。

translations.literal: Deploy your army with surprise forces and tactical changes, and report at once by memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Use your troops with surprise maneuvers and flexible tactics, and report back immediately by memorial.

sentences.zh: 又聞衍軍將帥，每有流言，云魏博淮陽、宿豫，乃是兩宜。

translations.literal: I have also heard that among the generals of Yan's army there are constant rumors saying that Weibo, Huaiyang, and Suyu would both be suitable targets.
translations.idiomatic: I have also heard persistent rumors among Yan's commanders that Weibo, Huaiyang, and Suyu would each make favorable objectives.

sentences.zh: 若實有此，卿可量朐山薪水得支幾時。

translations.literal: If this is indeed so, you may calculate how long the fuel and water supplies at Qiu Mountain can last.
translations.idiomatic: If those rumors are true, calculate how long the garrison at Qiu Mountain can sustain itself on its provisions.

sentences.zh: 脫事容往返，馳驛速聞。

translations.literal: If the situation would allow a round trip, report swiftly by express courier.
translations.idiomatic: If a round trip is feasible, send word back at once by express courier.

sentences.zh: 如薪水少急，即可量計。

translations.literal: If fuel and water are scarce and urgent, you may calculate and plan accordingly at once.
translations.idiomatic: If provisions are running critically low, assess the situation and act accordingly without delay.

sentences.zh: 若理不可爾，亦將軍裁決。」

translations.literal: If in principle it cannot be so, the decision shall also rest with the general."
translations.idiomatic: If the plan is not feasible, you as commander shall make the final decision."

sentences.zh: 昶既儒生，本少將略，又羊祉子燮為昶司馬，專任戎事，掩昶耳目，將士怨之。

translations.literal: Chang was by nature a scholar and originally had little knowledge of military strategy; moreover Yang Zhi's son Xie served as Chang's major, monopolizing military affairs and keeping Chang in the dark, and the officers and soldiers resented this.
translations.idiomatic: Chang was a scholar by training and had little military experience; moreover, Yang Zhi's son Xie served as his major, monopolized all military affairs, and kept Chang in the dark, to the resentment of officers and men alike.

sentences.zh: 朐山戍主傅文驥糧樵俱罄，以城降衍。

translations.literal: Fu Wenji, commander of the Qiu Mountain garrison, exhausted both grain and firewood and surrendered the city to Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Wenji, commander of the Qiu Mountain garrison, ran out of grain and firewood and surrendered the city to Yan.

sentences.zh: 昶見城降，於是先走退。

translations.literal: When Chang saw the city surrender, he thereupon fled first in retreat.
translations.idiomatic: When Chang saw the city had fallen, he was the first to flee.

sentences.zh: 諸軍相尋奔遁，遇大寒雪，軍人凍死及落手足者三分而二。

translations.literal: The various armies fled one after another; encountering bitter cold and heavy snow, two-thirds of the soldiers either froze to death or lost hands and feet.
translations.idiomatic: The armies broke and fled in succession; caught in bitter cold and heavy snow, two-thirds of the men either froze to death or lost hands and feet to frostbite.

sentences.zh: 自國家經略江左，唯有中山王英敗於鍾離，昶於朐山失利，最為甚焉。

translations.literal: Since the state began its campaigns against the lands south of the Yangtze, only the Prince of Zhongshan Ying's defeat at Zhongli and Chang's setback at Qiu Mountain have been so severe.
translations.idiomatic: Since the dynasty began its campaigns south of the Yangtze, only the Prince of Zhongshan Ying's defeat at Zhongli and Chang's loss at Qiu Mountain have been so disastrous.

sentences.zh: 世宗遣黃門甄琛馳驛鎖昶，窮其敗狀。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanwu dispatched the palace attendant Zhen Chen by express courier to place Chang in chains and thoroughly investigate the circumstances of the defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanwu sent the palace attendant Zhen Chen by express courier to arrest Chang in chains and investigate the defeat in full.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「朐山之敗，傷損實深，推始究末，罪鍾元帥。

translations.literal: An edict said: "The defeat at Qiu Mountain caused truly deep harm; tracing the beginning and examining the end, the guilt rests with the commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: An edict said: "The defeat at Qiu Mountain caused grave losses; tracing events from start to finish, the blame falls on the commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 雖經大宥，輕重宜別，昶一人可以免官論坐，自餘將統以下悉聽依赦復任。」

translations.literal: Although there has been a great amnesty, lighter and heavier punishments should be distinguished; Chang alone may be punished by removal from office, while all other commanders and officers below may resume their posts according to the pardon."
translations.idiomatic: Although a general amnesty has been proclaimed, punishments should vary in severity: Chang alone shall be stripped of office and held accountable, while all other commanders and officers may return to their posts under the pardon."

sentences.zh: 未幾，拜太常卿，仍除安西將軍、雍州刺史，又進號鎮西將軍，加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed Minister of Ceremonies, and concurrently made General Who Pacifies the West and Governor of Yong Province; he was further promoted to General Who Guards the West and given the additional title of Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was appointed Minister of Ceremonies and concurrently made General Who Pacifies the West and Governor of Yong Province; he was later promoted to General Who Guards the West with the additional title of Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 熙平元年卒於官。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xiping he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office in the first year of the Xiping era.

sentences.zh: 贈征北將軍、冀州刺史，諡曰穆。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted the title General Who Campaigns North and Governor of Ji Province, with the posthumous name Mu.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as General Who Campaigns North and Governor of Ji Province, with the posthumous name Mu.

sentences.zh: 昶寬和矜恕，善於綏撫，其在徐州，戍兵疾，親自檢恤。

translations.literal: Chang was generous, gentle, and forgiving, skilled at pacification and comfort; when he was in Xu Province and garrison soldiers fell ill, he personally inspected and cared for them.
translations.idiomatic: Chang was generous, gentle, and forgiving, and skilled at winning people over; while serving in Xu Province, when garrison soldiers fell ill, he personally visited and tended them.

sentences.zh: 至番兵年滿不歸，容充後役，終昶一政，然後始還。

translations.literal: When foreign troops whose terms had expired did not return home, he allowed them to serve additional rotations and only permitted their departure after his entire tenure had ended.
translations.idiomatic: When foreign troops whose terms had expired wished to stay, he allowed them to serve additional rotations and released them only after his entire term of office was complete.

sentences.zh: 人庶稱之。

translations.literal: The people praised him for this.
translations.idiomatic: The people praised him for it.

sentences.zh: 子元聿，字仲訓，無他才能。

translations.literal: His son Yuan Yu, courtesy name Zhongxun, had no other special talents.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yuan Yu, courtesy name Zhongxun, had no notable talents.

sentences.zh: 尚高祖女義陽長公主，拜駙馬都尉。

translations.literal: He married the Long Princess of Yiyang, a daughter of Emperor Gaozu, and was appointed Commandant of the Horse Guards for the Emperor's Sons-in-Law.
translations.idiomatic: He married the Long Princess of Yiyang, a daughter of Emperor Gaozu, and was appointed Commandant of the Horse Guards for Imperial Sons-in-Law.

sentences.zh: 位太尉司馬、光祿大夫。

translations.literal: He held the posts of Major of the Grand Commandant and Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to the posts of Major of the Grand Commandant and Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈中書監。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously granted the title Supervisor of the Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Upon his death he was posthumously honored as Supervisor of the Palace Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 子士晟，儀同開府掾。

translations.literal: His son Shi Sheng served as an aide in an office of equal rank to a grand commandant's establishment.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shi Sheng served as an aide in a grand commandant's establishment.

sentences.zh: 元聿第五弟元明，字幼章。

translations.literal: Yuan Yu's fifth younger brother Yuan Ming, courtesy name Youzhang.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Yu's fifth younger brother was Yuan Ming, courtesy name Youzhang.

sentences.zh: 涉歷羣書，兼有文義，風彩閒潤，進退可觀。

translations.literal: He ranged widely through many books and possessed both literary learning and moral understanding; his bearing was refined and graceful, and his conduct in all situations was admirable.
translations.idiomatic: He read widely and possessed both literary skill and moral discernment; his bearing was refined and graceful, and his conduct in every setting was admirable.

sentences.zh: 永安初，長兼尚書令、臨淮王彧欽愛之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Yong'an era, Yu, Prince of Linhuai, who long held the concurrent post of Director of the Masters of Writing, held him in high esteem.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Yong'an era, Yu, Prince of Linhuai, who long served concurrently as Director of the Masters of Writing, held him in high regard.

sentences.zh: 及彧開府，引為兼屬，仍領部曲。

translations.literal: When Yu opened his grand commandant's establishment, he brought Ming in as a concurrent staff member and also put him in charge of his personal troops.
translations.idiomatic: When Yu established his grand commandant's office, he brought Ming onto his staff and also placed him in command of his personal troops.

sentences.zh: 出帝登阼，以郎任行禮，封城陽縣子，遷中書侍郎。

translations.literal: When Emperor Chu ascended the throne, Ming served as a gentleman attendant in the accession ceremonies, was enfeoffed as Viscount of Chengyang County, and was promoted to Gentleman of the Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Chu ascended the throne, Ming served as a gentleman attendant in the accession rites, was enfeoffed as Viscount of Chengyang County, and was promoted to Gentleman of the Palace Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 永熙末，居洛東緱山，乃作幽居賦焉。

translations.literal: At the end of the Yongxi era he lived on Mount Gou east of Luoyang and there composed his "Rhapsody on Secluded Dwelling."
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Yongxi era he retired to Mount Gou east of Luoyang, where he wrote his "Rhapsody on Secluded Dwelling."

sentences.zh: 於時元明友人王由居潁川，忽夢由攜酒就之言別，賦詩為贈。

translations.literal: At that time Ming's friend Wang You was living in Yingchuan; suddenly Ming dreamed that You came bearing wine to bid farewell and composed a poem as a parting gift.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Ming's friend Wang You was living in Yingchuan; Ming suddenly dreamed that You came with wine to say farewell and composed a poem as a parting gift.

sentences.zh: 及明，憶其詩十字云：「自茲一去後，市朝不復遊。

translations.literal: When dawn came he recalled the poem's ten characters: "From this departure onward, I shall no longer roam the markets and courts.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn he recalled the poem's ten characters: "From this departure onward, I shall no longer walk the markets and courts of the world.

sentences.zh: 」元明歎曰：「由性不狎俗，旅寄人間，乃今有夢，又復如此，[7]必有他故。

translations.literal: "] Ming sighed and said: "You by nature does not consort with the vulgar world and lives as a sojourner among men; now to have such a dream again—there must be some other cause.
translations.idiomatic: " Ming sighed and said: "You by nature shuns worldly company and lives as a wanderer among men; to have such a dream now can only mean something has happened.

sentences.zh: 」經三日，果聞由為亂兵所害。

translations.literal: "] After three days he indeed heard that You had been killed by mutinous soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: " Three days later he learned that You had indeed been killed by mutinous soldiers.

sentences.zh: 尋其亡日，乃是得夢之夜。

translations.literal: When he traced the date of You's death, it was the very night he had received the dream.
translations.idiomatic: When he traced the date of You's death, it proved to be the very night of the dream.

sentences.zh: 天平中，兼吏部郎中，副李諧使蕭衍，南人稱之。

translations.literal: During the Tianping era he served concurrently as a Gentleman of the Ministry of Personnel and, as Li He's deputy, was sent on a mission to Xiao Yan; the southerners praised him.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianping era he served concurrently as a Gentleman of the Ministry of Personnel and, as Li He's deputy, went on a mission to Xiao Yan; the southerners spoke well of him.

sentences.zh: 還，拜尚書右丞，轉散騎常侍，監起居。

translations.literal: Upon his return he was appointed Right Assistant Director of the Masters of Writing, then transferred to Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and Supervisor of the Imperial Diary.
translations.idiomatic: After his return he was appointed Right Assistant Director of the Masters of Writing, then transferred to Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and Supervisor of the Imperial Diary.

sentences.zh: 積年在史館，了不厝意。

translations.literal: He spent many years in the Historiography Office and paid it no attention at all.
translations.idiomatic: He spent many years in the Historiography Office and gave the work no attention whatsoever.

sentences.zh: 又兼黃門郎、本州大中正。

translations.literal: He also served concurrently as a Gentleman of the Yellow Gate and as the chief arbiter of his native province.
translations.idiomatic: He also served concurrently as a Gentleman of the Yellow Gate and as chief provincial arbiter of his native commandery.

sentences.zh: 元明善自標置，不妄交遊，飲酒賦詩，遇興忘返。

translations.literal: Ming knew well how to set himself apart; he did not associate casually, and when drinking wine and composing poetry he would forget to return whenever inspiration seized him.
translations.idiomatic: Ming knew how to hold himself with dignity; he did not socialize lightly, and when drinking and composing poetry he would lose himself in the moment and forget to return home.

sentences.zh: 性好玄理，作史子新論數十篇，文筆別有集錄。

translations.literal: By nature he loved arcane philosophy and wrote several dozen chapters of New Discourses on the Historians and Philosophers; his literary writings were separately collected in a compilation.
translations.idiomatic: He had a natural love of philosophical speculation and wrote several dozen chapters of New Discourses on the Historians and Philosophers; his literary works were collected in a separate volume.

sentences.zh: 少時常從鄉還洛，途遇相州刺史、中山王熙。

translations.literal: In his youth, while returning from his home district to Luoyang, he encountered on the road Xi, Prince of Zhongshan and Governor of Xiang Province.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth, while traveling from his home district back to Luoyang, he met Xi, Prince of Zhongshan and Governor of Xiang Province, on the road.

sentences.zh: 熙博識之士，見而歎曰：「盧郎有如此風神，唯須誦離騷，飲美酒，自為佳器。

translations.literal: Xi was a man of broad learning; seeing Ming he sighed and said: "Young Master Lu has such spirit and bearing—he need only recite the "Li Sao," drink fine wine, and he will be a vessel of excellence in himself.
translations.idiomatic: Xi was a man of wide learning; seeing Ming, he sighed and said: "Young Master Lu has such spirit and bearing—all he need do is recite the "Li Sao," drink fine wine, and he will be a man of rare quality.

sentences.zh: 」遂留之數日，贈帛及馬而別。

translations.literal: "] He thereupon kept Ming for several days, then presented him with silk and a horse before they parted.
translations.idiomatic: " He kept Ming for several days, then presented him with silk and a horse before they parted.

sentences.zh: 元明凡三娶，次妻鄭氏與元明兄子士啟淫汙，元明不能離絕。

translations.literal: Ming married three times in all; his second wife, Lady Zheng, had an illicit affair with Ming's elder brother's son Shi Qi, and Ming could not bring himself to sever the relationship.
translations.idiomatic: Ming married three times in all; his second wife, Lady Zheng, had an affair with Ming's nephew Shi Qi, and Ming could not bring himself to cast her off.

sentences.zh: 又好以世地自矜，時論以此貶之。

translations.literal: He also liked to take pride in his family's standing, and contemporary opinion lowered its estimate of him for this.
translations.idiomatic: He also took excessive pride in his family's status, and contemporary opinion counted this against him.

sentences.zh: 元明弟元緝，字幼緒。

translations.literal: Ming's younger brother Yuan Ji, courtesy name Youxu.
translations.idiomatic: Ming's younger brother was Yuan Ji, courtesy name Youxu.

sentences.zh: 凶率好酒，曾於婦氏飲宴，小有不平，手刃其客。

translations.literal: He was fierce, reckless, and fond of wine; once while feasting at his wife's family's home, he took slight offense and killed a guest with his own hand.
translations.idiomatic: He was fierce, reckless, and fond of wine; once while feasting at his wife's family's home, he took slight offense and killed a guest with his own hand.

sentences.zh: 起家祕書郎，轉司徒祭酒。

translations.literal: He began his career as a Gentleman of the Palace Library and was transferred to Libationer of the Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: He began his career as a Gentleman of the Palace Library and was transferred to Libationer of the Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 稍遷輔國將軍、司徒司馬，卒於官。

translations.literal: He was gradually promoted to General Who Assists the State and Major of the Minister of Education, and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He was gradually promoted to General Who Assists the State and Major of the Minister of Education, and died in office.

sentences.zh: 贈散騎常侍、都督幽瀛二州諸軍事、驃騎大將軍、吏部尚書、幽州刺史，諡曰宣。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted the titles Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, Commander-in-Chief of All Military Affairs in You and Ying Provinces, General of Fast Cavalry, Director of the Ministry of Personnel, and Governor of You Province, with the posthumous name Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, Commander-in-Chief of All Military Affairs in You and Ying Provinces, General of Fast Cavalry, Director of the Ministry of Personnel, and Governor of You Province, with the posthumous name Xuan.

sentences.zh: 子士深，開府行參軍。

translations.literal: His son Shi Shen served as a traveling aide in a grand commandant's establishment.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shi Shen served as a traveling aide in a grand commandant's establishment.

sentences.zh: 昶弟尚之，字季儒，小字羨夏，亦以儒素見重。

translations.literal: Chang's younger brother Shangzhi, courtesy name Jiru and childhood name Xianxia, was also esteemed for his scholarly integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Chang's younger brother Shangzhi, courtesy name Jiru and childhood name Xianxia, was likewise respected for his scholarly integrity.

sentences.zh: 太和中，拜議郎，轉趙郡王征東諮議參軍。

translations.literal: During the Taihe era he was appointed Gentleman Consultant and transferred to Strategic Adviser on the staff of the Prince of Zhao Commandery, Commander Who Campaigns East.
translations.idiomatic: During the Taihe era he was appointed Gentleman Consultant and transferred to Strategic Adviser on the staff of the Prince of Zhao Commandery, Commander Who Campaigns East.

sentences.zh: 母憂去官。

translations.literal: He left office upon his mother's death.
translations.idiomatic: He left office to observe mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 後為太尉主簿、司徒屬、范陽太守、章武內史、兼司徒右長史，加冠軍將軍，轉左長史。

translations.literal: Later he served as Chief Clerk to the Grand Commandant, an official of the Minister of Education, Governor of Fanyang, Internal Administrator of Zhangwu, and concurrently Right Chief Clerk of the Minister of Education; he was given the additional title General Who Establishes Victory and was transferred to Left Chief Clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Later he served as Chief Clerk to the Grand Commandant, an official of the Minister of Education, Governor of Fanyang, Internal Administrator of Zhangwu, and concurrently Right Chief Clerk of the Minister of Education; he was given the additional title General Who Establishes Victory and was transferred to Left Chief Clerk.

sentences.zh: 出為前將軍、濟州刺史。

translations.literal: He was sent out as General of the Vanguard and Governor of Ji Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out to serve as General of the Vanguard and Governor of Ji Province.

sentences.zh: 入除光祿大夫。

translations.literal: He was recalled and appointed Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to court and appointed Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 正光五年卒，年六十二。

translations.literal: He died in the fifth year of Zhengguang at the age of sixty-two.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fifth year of the Zhengguang era at the age of sixty-two.

sentences.zh: 贈散騎常侍、安東將軍、青州刺史。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted the titles Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, General Who Pacifies the East, and Governor of Qing Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, General Who Pacifies the East, and Governor of Qing Province.

sentences.zh: 長子文甫，字元祐。

translations.literal: His eldest son Wenfu, courtesy name Yuanyou.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son was Wenfu, courtesy name Yuanyou.

sentences.zh: 少有器尚，涉歷文史，有譽於時。

translations.literal: From youth he possessed ability and high aspiration, ranged through literature and history, and enjoyed a reputation in his time.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he showed ability and high aspiration, read widely in literature and history, and enjoyed a fine reputation in his day.

sentences.zh: 位司空參軍，年四十九卒。

translations.literal: He held the post of Aide to the Minister of Works and died at the age of forty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Aide to the Minister of Works and died at the age of forty-nine.

sentences.zh: 子敬舒，有文學，早亡。

translations.literal: His son Jingshu had literary talent and died young.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jingshu was a man of letters and died young.

sentences.zh: 文甫弟文翼，字仲祐。

translations.literal: Wenfu's younger brother Wenyi, courtesy name Zhongyou.
translations.idiomatic: Wenfu's younger brother was Wenyi, courtesy name Zhongyou.

sentences.zh: 少甚輕躁，晚頗改節。

translations.literal: In youth he was very frivolous and impetuous; in later years he changed his ways considerably.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he was very frivolous and impetuous; in later years he reformed his conduct considerably.

sentences.zh: 為員外郎，因歸鄉里。

translations.literal: He served as an External Gentleman and then returned to his home district.
translations.idiomatic: He served as an External Gentleman and then returned to his home district.

sentences.zh: 永安中，為都督，守范陽三城，拒賊帥韓婁有功，賜爵范陽子。

translations.literal: During the Yong'an era he served as commander, defended the three cities of Fanyang, and had merit in repelling the bandit chief Han Lou; he was granted the title Viscount of Fanyang.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yong'an era he served as commander, defended the three cities of Fanyang, and distinguished himself repelling the bandit chief Han Lou; he was enfeoffed as Viscount of Fanyang.

sentences.zh: 永熙中，除右將軍、太中大夫。

translations.literal: During the Yongxi era he was appointed General of the Right and Grand Master of Palace Counsel.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yongxi era he was appointed General of the Right and Grand Master of Palace Counsel.

sentences.zh: 栖遲桑井而卒，年六十。

translations.literal: He lived out his days in his native village and died at the age of sixty.
translations.idiomatic: He lived out his days in his native village and died at the age of sixty.

sentences.zh: 子士偉，興和中，中散大夫。

translations.literal: His son Shi Wei, during the Xinghe era, served as Palace Doctor.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shi Wei served as Palace Doctor during the Xinghe era.

sentences.zh: 子翼弟文符，字叔僖，性通率。

translations.literal: Wenyi's younger brother Wenfu, courtesy name Shuxi, was by nature straightforward and unpretentious.
translations.idiomatic: Wenyi's younger brother was Wenfu, courtesy name Shuxi, a straightforward and unpretentious man.

sentences.zh: 位員外郎、羽林監、尚書主客郎中，遷通直散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: He held the posts of External Gentleman, Supervisor of the Feathered Forest Guard, and Gentleman of the Masters of Writing in charge of foreign guests, and was promoted to Attendant Gentleman of the Palace Library.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the posts of External Gentleman, Supervisor of the Feathered Forest Guard, and Gentleman of the Masters of Writing in charge of foreign guests, and was promoted to Attendant Gentleman of the Palace Library.

sentences.zh: 永安中卒，年四十。

translations.literal: He died during the Yong'an era at the age of forty.
translations.idiomatic: He died during the Yong'an era at the age of forty.

sentences.zh: 子子潛，[8]武定中，齊文襄王中外府中兵參軍。

translations.literal: His son Ziqian, during the Wuding era, served as a military aide in the inner and outer establishment of Prince Wenxiang of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ziqian served during the Wuding era as a military aide in the inner and outer establishment of Prince Wenxiang of Qi.

sentences.zh: 度世，李氏之甥。

translations.literal: Dushi was a nephew on the maternal side of the Li clan.
translations.idiomatic: Dushi was a nephew of the Li clan on his mother's side.

sentences.zh: 其為濟州也，[9]國家初平升城。

translations.literal: When he was Governor of Ji Province, the state had just pacified Shengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: While he was Governor of Ji Province, the dynasty had just pacified Shengcheng.

sentences.zh: 無鹽房崇吉母傅氏，度世繼外祖母兄之子婦也。

translations.literal: Lady Fu, mother of Fang Chongji of Wuyan, was the wife whom Dushi had taken in marriage from among the sons of his maternal grandmother's elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Fu, mother of Fang Chongji of Wuyan, was the wife Dushi had married from among his maternal grandmother's elder brother's descendants.

sentences.zh: 兗州刺史申纂妻賈氏，崇吉之姑女也，皆亡破軍途，老病憔悴。

translations.literal: Lady Jia, wife of Shen Zuan, Governor of Yan Province and paternal aunt's daughter of Chongji, had all been lost amid the turmoil of defeated armies on the road, old, ill, and worn with hardship.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Jia, wife of Shen Zuan, Governor of Yan Province and Chongji's cousin on his father's side, had been lost amid the chaos of retreating armies; both women were aged, ill, and worn with hardship.

sentences.zh: 而度世推計中表，致其恭恤。

translations.literal: Yet Dushi calculated their cousin relationships and extended to them his respectful care.
translations.idiomatic: Dushi traced their kinship ties and treated them with respectful devotion.

sentences.zh: 每覲見傅氏，跪問起居，隨時奉送衣被食物，亦存賑賈氏，供其服膳。

translations.literal: Whenever he visited Lady Fu he knelt to inquire after her health and, as the seasons turned, presented her with clothing, bedding, and food; he also looked after and relieved Lady Jia and provided for her clothing and meals.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he visited Lady Fu he knelt to inquire after her health and sent her clothing, bedding, and food as the seasons required; he also cared for Lady Jia and provided for her clothing and meals.

sentences.zh: 青州既陷，諸崔墜落，多所收贖。

translations.literal: After Qing Province fell, many members of the Cui clan were cast down, and he ransomed a great many of them.
translations.idiomatic: After Qing Province fell, many members of the Cui clan were reduced to destitution, and he ransomed a great number of them.

sentences.zh: 及淵、昶等並循父風，遠親疏屬，敍為尊行，長者莫不畢拜致敬。

translations.literal: Yuan, Chang, and the others all followed their father's example; distant and close kin alike they ranked as elders in the family hierarchy, and none of the seniors failed to receive their full bows and respect.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan, Chang, and the others all followed their father's example: whether kin were near or far, they were ranked by seniority in the family, and every elder received their full bows and respect.

sentences.zh: 閨門之禮，為世所推。

translations.literal: The rites observed within their household were praised by the age.
translations.idiomatic: The rites observed within their household were admired throughout the land.

sentences.zh: 謙退簡約，不與世競。

translations.literal: They were humble, restrained, and simple, and did not compete with the world.
translations.idiomatic: They were humble, restrained, and unpretentious, and did not strive against the world.

sentences.zh: 父母亡，然同居共財，自祖至孫，家內百口。

translations.literal: After their parents died, they still lived together and shared their property; from grandfathers to grandsons, the household numbered a hundred mouths.
translations.idiomatic: After their parents died, they continued to live together and share their property; from grandfathers to grandsons, the household numbered a hundred mouths.

sentences.zh: 在洛時有飢年，無以自贍，然尊卑怡穆，豐儉同之。

translations.literal: While in Luoyang there were years of famine and they had no means to support themselves, yet young and old remained harmonious and serene, sharing alike in plenty and in want.
translations.idiomatic: While living in Luoyang they endured years of famine and could scarcely support themselves, yet young and old remained harmonious and serene, sharing alike in plenty and in want.

sentences.zh: 親從昆弟，常旦省謁諸父，出坐別室，至暮乃入。

translations.literal: The brothers among the close and collateral kin would each morning pay their respects to their uncles, then go out to sit in separate rooms and only enter again at dusk.
translations.idiomatic: Brothers among the close and collateral kin would each morning pay their respects to their uncles, then withdraw to separate rooms and only rejoin the household at dusk.

sentences.zh: 朝府之外，不妄交遊。

translations.literal: Outside the court and government offices, they did not form friendships rashly.
translations.idiomatic: Outside official circles they did not form casual friendships.

sentences.zh: 其相勗以禮如此。

translations.literal: Thus they exhorted one another with ritual propriety.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the way they urged one another to observe ritual propriety.

sentences.zh: 又一門三主，當世以為榮。

translations.literal: Moreover, three heads of household in one clan were regarded by their age as an honor.
translations.idiomatic: Three heads of household in a single clan were counted an honor in their day.

sentences.zh: 淵兄弟亡，及道將卒後，家風衰損，子孫多非法，帷薄混穢，為論者所鄙。

translations.literal: After Yuan and his brothers died, and after Dao Jiang died as well, the family ethos declined; many descendants acted unlawfully, and disorder within the women's quarters became foul—men of judgment despised them for it.
translations.idiomatic: After Yuan and his brothers passed away, and after Dao Jiang died as well, the family's standards fell away; many descendants broke the law, and scandal spread within the inner household, so that critics held them in contempt.

sentences.zh: 度世從祖弟神寶，中書博士。

translations.literal: Du Shi's cousin Shenbao served as Doctor of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Du Shi's cousin Shenbao was a Doctor of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 太和中，高祖為高陽王雍納其女為妃。

translations.literal: In the Taihe era, Gaozu took his daughter as consort for the Prince of Gaoyang, Yong.
translations.idiomatic: During the Taihe era, Emperor Gaozu had his daughter marry Prince Yong of Gaoyang as his consort.

sentences.zh: 初，玄從祖兄溥，慕容寶之末，總攝鄉部，屯於海濱，遂殺其鄉姻諸祖十餘人，稱征北大將軍、幽州刺史，攻掠郡縣。

translations.literal: Earlier, Xuan's cousin Pu, at the end of Murong Bao's reign, took overall charge of the district communities and encamped on the seacoast; he then killed more than ten elders among his local kin by marriage, styled himself General Who Campaigns North and Governor of You Province, and raided commanderies and counties.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Xuan's cousin Pu, in the last days of Murong Bao, took charge of the local communities and encamped on the coast; he killed more than ten senior kinsmen of his district, styled himself General Who Campaigns North and Governor of You Province, and raided the commanderies.

sentences.zh: 天興中討禽之，事在帝紀。

translations.literal: In the Tianxing era he was captured in punitive action; the affair is recorded in the imperial annals.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tianxing era he was captured in a punitive campaign; the affair is recorded in the imperial annals.

sentences.zh: 溥玄孫洪，字曾孫。

translations.literal: Pu's great-grandson Hong bore the style name Zengsun.
translations.idiomatic: Pu's great-grandson Hong, style name Zengsun.

sentences.zh: 太和中，歷中書博士，稍遷高陽王雍鎮北府諮議參軍、幽州中正、樂陵陽平二郡太守。

translations.literal: In the Taihe era he served as Doctor of the Secretariat, was gradually promoted to Advisory Officer in the Northern Defense Staff of Prince Yong of Gaoyang, Chief Rectifier of You Province, and Governor of the two commanderies of Leling and Yangping.
translations.idiomatic: During the Taihe era he served as Doctor of the Secretariat, then rose to Advisory Officer on Prince Yong of Gaoyang's northern staff, Chief Rectifier of You Province, and Governor of Leling and Yangping commanderies.

sentences.zh: 洪三子。

translations.literal: Hong had three sons.
translations.idiomatic: Hong had three sons.

sentences.zh: 長子崇，字元禮。

translations.literal: The eldest son Chong bore the style name Yuanli.
translations.idiomatic: The eldest son Chong, style name Yuanli.

sentences.zh: 少立美名，有識者許之以遠大。

translations.literal: From youth he established a fine reputation; men of discernment predicted great things for him.
translations.idiomatic: He won a fine reputation early on, and men of judgment foresaw a brilliant future for him.

sentences.zh: 景明中，驃騎府法曹參軍。

translations.literal: In the Jingming era he served as Legal Bureau Officer in the Rapid Cavalry Command.
translations.idiomatic: In the Jingming era he was Legal Bureau Officer in the Rapid Cavalry Command.

sentences.zh: 早卒。

translations.literal: He died young.
translations.idiomatic: He died young.

sentences.zh: 子子剛，司空行參軍、荊州驃騎府主簿。

translations.literal: His son Zigang served as Acting Staff Officer to the Minister of Works and Chief Clerk in the Rapid Cavalry Command of Jing Province.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zigang was Acting Staff Officer to the Minister of Works and Chief Clerk in the Jing Province Rapid Cavalry Command.

sentences.zh: 沒於關中。

translations.literal: He perished in Guanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: He perished in Guanzhong.

sentences.zh: 崇弟仲義，小名黑，知名於世。
