translations.literal: Chong's younger brother Zhongyi, childhood name Hei, was known throughout the world.
translations.idiomatic: Chong's younger brother Zhongyi, called Hei as a child, was famous in his time.

sentences.zh: 高陽王雍司空行參軍、員外散騎侍郎、幽州別駕。

translations.literal: He served as Acting Staff Officer to Prince Yong of Gaoyang when the latter was Minister of Works, Extraordinary Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, and Vice Governor of You Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was Acting Staff Officer to Prince Yong of Gaoyang as Minister of Works, Extraordinary Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, and Vice Governor of You Province.

sentences.zh: 弟三子叔矩，字子規。

translations.literal: The third son Shuju bore the style name Zigui.
translations.idiomatic: The third son Shuju, style name Zigui.

sentences.zh: 武定中，尚書郎。

translations.literal: In the Wuding era he was a Gentleman of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: In the Wuding era he was a Gentleman of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 子規弟子正，司徒法曹參軍。

translations.literal: Zigui's nephew Zizheng served as Legal Bureau Officer under the Minister of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Zigui's nephew Zizheng was Legal Bureau Officer under the Minister of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 崇兄弟官雖不達，至於婚姻，常與玄家齊等。

translations.literal: Though Chong and his brothers did not rise high in office, in marriage alliances they were regularly ranked equal to Xuan's line.
translations.idiomatic: Though Chong and his brothers never rose to high office, in marriage they were regularly matched with Xuan's branch as equals.

sentences.zh: 仲義弟幹，字幼禎。

translations.literal: Zhongyi's younger brother Gan bore the style name Youzhen.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongyi's younger brother Gan, style name Youzhen.

sentences.zh: 州主簿。

translations.literal: He was Chief Clerk of the province.
translations.idiomatic: He was Chief Clerk of the province.

sentences.zh: 子讓，儀同開府參軍。

translations.literal: His son Rang served as Staff Officer in an Equipage-on-Par Opening Command.
translations.idiomatic: His son Rang was Staff Officer in an Equipage-on-Par Opening Command.

sentences.zh: 洪弟光宗，子觀，觀弟仲宣，事在文苑傳。

translations.literal: Hong's younger brother Guangzong, his son Guan, and Guan's younger brother Zhongxuan—their affairs are recorded in the Treatise on Literature and Gardens.
translations.idiomatic: Hong's younger brother Guangzong, his son Guan, and Guan's younger brother Zhongxuan are treated in the Treatise on Literature and Gardens.

sentences.zh: 仲宣弟叔虎，[10]武定初，司徒諮議參軍。

translations.literal: Zhongxuan's younger brother Shuhu,[10] in early Wuding, served as Advisory Officer under the Minister of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongxuan's younger brother Shuhu,[10] in early Wuding, was Advisory Officer under the Minister of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 洪從弟附伯，附伯弟侍伯，並有學識。

translations.literal: Hong's cousins Fubo and Shibo both possessed learning and discernment.
translations.idiomatic: Hong's cousins Fubo and Shibo were both men of learning.

sentences.zh: 附伯位至滄州平東府長史。

translations.literal: Fubo rose to Chief Clerk of the Eastern Pacification Staff in Cang Province.
translations.idiomatic: Fubo rose to Chief Clerk of the Eastern Pacification Staff in Cang Province.

sentences.zh: 侍伯，永熙中衞大將軍、南岐州刺史。

translations.literal: Shibo, in the Yongxi era, was General of the Guard and Governor of Southern Qi Province.
translations.idiomatic: Shibo, in the Yongxi era, was General of the Guard and Governor of Southern Qi Province.

sentences.zh: 侍伯從弟文偉，興和中，驃騎大將軍、青州刺史、大夏縣開國男。

translations.literal: Shibo's cousin Wenwei, in the Xinghe era, was General of Rapid Cavalry, Governor of Qing Province, and Baron of the founding fief of Daxia County.
translations.idiomatic: Shibo's cousin Wenwei, in the Xinghe era, was General of Rapid Cavalry, Governor of Qing Province, and founding Baron of Daxia County.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：盧玄緒業著聞，首應旌命，子孫繼迹，為世盛門。

translations.literal: The historiographer states: Lu Xuan's inherited enterprise was renowned; he was the first to answer the imperial summons, and his descendants continued his path, becoming a great house of the age.
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer writes: Lu Xuan's inherited standing was illustrious; he was the first to answer the imperial call, and his descendants followed in his steps, making the Lu clan a great house of their age.

sentences.zh: 其文武功烈，殆無足紀，而見重於時，聲高冠帶，蓋德業儒素有過人者。

translations.literal: Their literary and military achievements and blazing merit were scarcely worth recording, yet they were esteemed in their time and their fame towered among the gentry—surely their virtue, conduct, and Confucian cultivation surpassed ordinary men.
translations.idiomatic: Their literary and military exploits were hardly worth chronicling in themselves, yet they were held in honor and their fame rang among the gentry—surely it was their virtue and scholarly cultivation that set them apart.

sentences.zh: 淵之兄弟亦有二方之風流。

translations.literal: Yuan's brothers likewise possessed the elegance of the two capitals.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan's brothers too had something of the cultivated grace of the two capitals.

sentences.zh: 雅道家聲，諸子不逮，餘烈所被，弗及盈乎？

translations.literal: The refined reputation of the family—could the sons match it? Could the lingering glory they spread ever fill the measure?
translations.idiomatic: The refined renown of the house—could their sons equal it? Could the afterglow of their fame ever quite fill the cup?

sentences.zh: 定火之雄 李慈銘云：「『火』字有誤，蓋謂太武親征赫連定事也。」

translations.literal: The hero who settled the fire—Li Ciming states: "The character 'fire' is in error; it likely refers to Emperor Taiwu's personal campaign against Helian Ding."
translations.idiomatic: The hero who settled the fire—Li Ciming remarks: "The character huo is mistaken; the passage surely refers to Emperor Taiwu's personal expedition against Helian Ding."

sentences.zh: 而道將引清河王國常侍韓子熙讓弟仲穆魯陽男之例 諸本「王國」誤倒作「國王」，今據北史卷三０盧玄附盧道將傳乙正。

translations.literal: Dao Jiang cited the precedent of Han Zixi, Regular Attendant of the Prince of Qinghe's kingdom, yielding to his younger brother Zhongmu, Baron of Luyang—in various editions "prince's kingdom" is wrongly reversed as "kingdom prince"; the text is now corrected according to the biography of Lu Dao Jiang appended to Lu Xuan in Northern History, juan 30.
translations.idiomatic: Dao Jiang cited Han Zixi's precedent of yielding his title to his younger brother Zhongmu—in various editions wangguo is wrongly reversed as guowang; the reading is corrected here from the biography of Lu Dao Jiang in Northern History, juan 30.

sentences.zh: 道將弟亮字仁業 北史卷三０盧玄附盧淵傳「亮」上有「道」字，「仁業」作「仲業」。

translations.literal: Dao Jiang's younger brother Liang, style name Renye—in Northern History, juan 30, biography of Lu Yuan appended to Lu Xuan, the character dao precedes Liang, and Renye is written Zhongye.
translations.idiomatic: Dao Jiang's younger brother Liang, style name Renye—in Northern History, juan 30, the name reads Dao Liang and the style name is Zhongye rather than Renye.

sentences.zh: 張森楷云：「道將兄弟八人並以『道』字為次，不應亮獨無之，疑此當誤脫文。

translations.literal: Zhang Senkai states: "Dao Jiang's eight brothers all take the character dao in their generation names; Liang alone should not lack it—this is suspected to be a mistaken omission in the text."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Senkai remarks: "All eight of Dao Jiang's brothers bear the generation character dao; Liang alone should not lack it—this looks like a textual omission."

sentences.zh: 『仲』『仁』二字，未知孰是。

translations.literal: Whether zhong or ren is correct in the style name is not known.
translations.idiomatic: Whether the style name should read Zhongye or Renye cannot be determined.

sentences.zh: 」按北齊書卷四二盧潛傳、隋書卷五七盧思道傳並作「道亮」。

translations.literal: According to the biography of Lu Qian in Northern Qi History, juan 42, and of Lu Sidao in Sui History, juan 57, both read Dao Liang.
translations.idiomatic: The biographies of Lu Qian in Northern Qi History, juan 42, and Lu Sidao in Sui History, juan 57, both give the name as Dao Liang.

sentences.zh: 這裏「亮」上當脫「道」字。

translations.literal: Here the character dao has dropped out before Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Here the character dao has been omitted before Liang.

sentences.zh: 下「亮弟道裕」同脫。

translations.literal: Below, in "Liang's younger brother Dao Yu," dao is likewise omitted.
translations.idiomatic: The same omission appears below in "Liang's younger brother Dao Yu."

sentences.zh: 道侃弟道和字叔維 北史卷三０「維」作「雍」。

translations.literal: Dao Kan's younger brother Dao He, style name Shuwei—in Northern History, juan 30, wei is written yong.
translations.idiomatic: Dao Kan's younger brother Dao He, style name Shuwei—in Northern History, juan 30, the final character is yong rather than wei.

sentences.zh: 張森楷云：「『雍』與『和』義洽，此形近而訛。」

translations.literal: Zhang Senkai states: "Yong harmonizes in meaning with He; this is a corruption through graphic similarity."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Senkai remarks: "Yong accords in meaning with He; this is a corruption through similar forms."

sentences.zh: 時復惠好 北史卷三０盧玄附盧義僖傳「好」作「存」，冊府卷六八七

translations.literal: From time to time showing kindness—in Northern History, juan 30, biography of Lu Yixi appended to Lu Xuan, hao is written cun; in Cefu, juan 687
translations.idiomatic: From time to time showing kindness—in Northern History, juan 30, hao is written cun; in Cefu, juan 687

sentences.zh: 〈八一八八頁〉

translations.literal: 〈page 8188〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈page 8188〉

sentences.zh: 作「來」。

translations.literal: it is written lai.
translations.idiomatic: the reading is lai (come).

sentences.zh: 疑作「存」是。

translations.literal: Cun is suspected to be correct.
translations.idiomatic: Cun is probably the correct reading.

sentences.zh: 邀憑雨熱 諸本「雨」作「兩」，獨局本作「雨」。

translations.literal: Relying on rain and heat—in various editions yu is written liang; only the Ju edition has yu.
translations.idiomatic: Relying on rain and heat—in most editions yu is written liang (two); only the Ju edition reads yu (rain).

sentences.zh: 按「兩熱」不可解。

translations.literal: Liang and re together make no sense.
translations.idiomatic: Liang re makes no sense.

sentences.zh: 局本當是以意改。

translations.literal: The Ju edition must have been altered according to the editor's understanding.
translations.idiomatic: The Ju edition was probably emended by conjecture.

sentences.zh: 據上文詔書有「水雨盛行」語，局本改「雨」是，今從之。

translations.literal: According to the edict above, which has the phrase "water and rain prevail widely," the Ju edition's change to yu is correct; it is followed here.
translations.idiomatic: Since the edict above speaks of floods and rain prevailing widely, the Ju edition's reading yu is correct and is adopted here.

sentences.zh: 又復如此 北史卷三０盧玄附盧元明傳「又」作「詩」。

translations.literal: Again just like this—in Northern History, juan 30, biography of Lu Yuanming appended to Lu Xuan, you is written shi.
translations.idiomatic: Again just like this—in Northern History, juan 30, you is written shi (poem).

sentences.zh: 李慈銘云：「『又』上脫『詩』字。」

translations.literal: Li Ciming states: "The character shi has dropped out before you."
translations.idiomatic: Li Ciming remarks: "The character shi has been omitted before you."

sentences.zh: 子子潛 北史卷三０盧玄附盧元明傳但云「子潛」。

translations.literal: Son Ziqian—in Northern History, juan 30, biography of Lu Yuanming appended to Lu Xuan, it reads only "son Qian."
translations.idiomatic: Son Ziqian—in Northern History, juan 30, the text reads only "son Qian."

sentences.zh: 按盧潛，北齊書卷四二有傳。

translations.literal: Lu Qian has a biography in Northern Qi History, juan 42.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Qian has a biography in Northern Qi History, juan 42.

sentences.zh: 這裏「潛」上當衍一「子」字。

translations.literal: Here the character zi has been added in error before Qian.
translations.idiomatic: Here the character zi before Qian is probably a scribal addition.

sentences.zh: 仲宣弟叔虎 諸本「虎」作「虔」，北史卷三０作「彪」。

translations.literal: Zhongxuan's younger brother Shuhu—in various editions hu is written qian; Northern History, juan 30, has biao.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongxuan's younger brother Shuhu—in most editions hu is written qian; Northern History, juan 30, reads biao.

sentences.zh: 按北齊書卷四二有盧叔武傳，即此人。

translations.literal: Northern Qi History, juan 42, has a biography of Lu Shuwu—this is the man.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Qi History, juan 42, has a biography of Lu Shuwu—this is the same man.

sentences.zh: 本是「虎」字，「彪」「武」都是避唐諱改，若本作「虔」，作「彪」作「武」便沒有理由。

translations.literal: The original character was hu; biao and wu are both changes to avoid Tang taboo—if the original reading were qian, there would be no reason to write biao or wu.
translations.idiomatic: The original reading was hu; biao and wu are both Tang taboo-avoidance forms—if the base text read qian, there would be no reason to change it to biao or wu.

sentences.zh: 知「虔」是「虎」的形訛，今改正。

translations.literal: Thus qian is a graphic corruption of hu; it is corrected here.
translations.idiomatic: Qian is therefore a graphic corruption of hu and is corrected here.
